-If the hour value is 0 or negative, the cookie expires immediately.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/storage

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../storage)*

# `storage.js` Module Documentation

`storage.js` is a CrootJS module for saving, reading, and deleting data in the browser's `localStorage` and `sessionStorage`. Unlike the built-in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, this module automatically performs `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse` (so you can store objects/arrays directly, not just strings), and its `localStorage` functions support optional expiry (days/hours/seconds) — something the built-in `localStorage` does not have.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { setLocal, getLocal, deleteLocal } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/storage.js";
```

## localStorage

### `setLocal(key, value)`
Saves data to `localStorage` with no expiry (it stays until it is deleted manually or the browser's storage is cleared). `value` can be a string, number, boolean, object, or array.

```javascript
setLocal("prefs", { theme: "dark", fontSize: 16 });
```

### `setLocalWithExpireDay(key, value, exdays)` / `setLocalWithExpireHour(key, value, exhour)` / `setLocalWithExpireSecond(key, value, exsecs)`
Saves data to `localStorage` with a validity period. Once that time has passed, `getLocal` automatically treats it as missing (and immediately removes it from storage).

```javascript
setLocalWithExpireHour("draftArtikel", { judul: "..." }, 2); // valid for 2 hours
```

### `getLocal(key)`
Reads data from `localStorage`. Returns `null` if the key does not exist, has expired, or its data is corrupt.

```javascript
const prefs = getLocal("prefs"); // { theme: "dark", fontSize: 16 } or null
```

### `deleteLocal(key)`
Deletes data from `localStorage`.

## sessionStorage

Same as above, but for `sessionStorage` (cleared automatically when the tab is closed) and without the expiry option (not relevant, because the browser already clears `sessionStorage` automatically):

- `setSession(key, value)`
- `getSession(key)`
- `deleteSession(key)`

```javascript
setSession("langkahForm", 2);
const langkah = getSession("langkahForm"); // 2
```

## Notes

- `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` are per-origin (domain) and cannot be accessed across domains.
- Data stored with this module (including data without expiry via `setLocal`) can still be deleted by the browser at any time (private/incognito mode, full storage, or the user clearing site data) — do not make it the only source of important data.
- If you need a cookie (sent to the server via an HTTP header), use [`cookie.js`](cookie), not this module — `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` can only be accessed from JavaScript and are not sent to the backend automatically.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/debounce

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../debounce)*

# `debounce.js` Module Documentation

`debounce.js` contains two wrapper functions (*higher-order functions*) that limit how often a function may run — useful for events that fire very frequently, such as typing, scroll, resize, or mousemove.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { debounce, throttle } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/debounce.js";
```

## `debounce(fn, delay)`

Delays running `fn` until the user **stops** triggering it for `delay` milliseconds. If it is called again before that time is up, the countdown restarts from the beginning. The result: `fn` runs only **once**, after the user is done (not in the middle).

**Most common use**: search-as-you-type — so a request is not sent to the server on every keystroke, only after the user stops typing.

```javascript
import { debounce } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/debounce.js";
import { onInput, getValue } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";
import { getJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/api.js";

const cariProduk = debounce(() => {
    const kata = getValue("kotakPencarian");
    getJSON(`https://api.example.com/produk?q=${kata}`, (res) => {
        console.log(res.data);
    });
}, 400); // wait 400ms after the user stops typing

onInput("kotakPencarian", cariProduk);
```

## `throttle(fn, delay)`

Limits `fn` so it runs **at most once** every `delay` milliseconds, even if it is triggered far more often than that. Unlike `debounce`, the first call runs immediately (*leading call*), and if there is a new trigger during the waiting period, the **last** call still runs after `delay` has passed (*trailing call*) — so the latest data is never lost.

**Most common use**: `scroll`/`resize`/`mousemove` events, which can fire dozens of times per second.

```javascript
import { throttle } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/debounce.js";

window.addEventListener("scroll", throttle(() => {
    console.log("scroll position:", window.scrollY);
}, 200)); // runs at most every 200ms
```

## Notes

- Both functions return a new, already-wrapped function — call `debounce(fn, delay)`/`throttle(fn, delay)` **once** outside the handler, then register the result as the listener (as in the examples above). Do not call `debounce(...)`/`throttle(...)` inside the handler itself, because that creates a new wrapper every time and cancels out the effect.
- `this` and all of the original call's arguments are passed through to `fn`.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/toast

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../toast)*

# `toast.js` Module Documentation

`toast.js` shows small notifications (*toasts*) in the top-right corner of the screen — with no external dependencies at all. Its CSS is *injected* automatically by the module itself, only once (not written by hand in your project's HTML/CSS), so importing this one file is all you need to start using it.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { toast, toastSuccess, toastError, toastWarning, toastInfo } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/toast.js";
```

## `toast(message, type = "info", duration = 3000)`

Shows one toast. `type` determines the color: `"info"` (blue, default), `"success"` (green), `"error"` (red), `"warning"` (yellow). `duration` is in milliseconds — the toast disappears automatically after it. If `duration` is set to `0`, the toast does **not** disappear automatically (it has to be dismissed manually).

Returns a `dismiss()` function — call it at any time to close that toast manually, even before `duration` has elapsed.

```javascript
toast("Data berhasil disimpan"); // info, disappears automatically after 3 seconds
toast("Berhasil!", "success", 2000);
toast("Gagal mengirim data", "error");
```

## Shortcut Functions

Same as `toast()` but with the type already set — you only need to provide `message` and (optionally) `duration`:

```javascript
toastSuccess("Berhasil disimpan!");
toastError("Terjadi kesalahan, coba lagi.");
toastWarning("Koneksi lambat...");
toastInfo("Memuat data...");
```

## Manually dismissed toast (e.g. a loading state)

```javascript
import { toastInfo } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/toast.js";
import { postJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/api.js";

const tutupLoading = toastInfo("Mengunggah...", 0); // duration 0 = does not disappear on its own

postJSON("https://api.example.com/upload", data, (res) => {
    tutupLoading(); // close the loading toast once finished
    if (res.status === 200) {
        toastSuccess("Berhasil diunggah!");
    } else {
        toastError("Gagal mengunggah.");
    }
});
```

## Notes

- The toast styles (colors, position, animation) are *injected* automatically as a single `<style id="crootjs-toast-style">` in `<head>` when the first toast is shown — this is part of how the module works, not a style you need to (or should) write by hand in your project's CSS file.
- If you need a confirmation dialog (with OK/Cancel buttons), this module is not meant for that — `toast.js` is only for brief notifications that do not require user interaction.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/geo

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../geo)*

# `geo.js` Module Documentation

`geo.js` is the CrootJS module for reading geospatial data. The currently supported format is **GeoJSON** ([RFC 7946](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946)): fetch it from a URL, read it from a file the user picks, validate it, then summarize its contents (bounding box, center point, property names).

Whatever the data's source and shape, the result you receive is always the same: a `FeatureCollection` in which every feature has `properties` as an object. So the code that follows only needs to be written for one shape.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { getGeoJSON, getBBox, getPropertyKeys } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geo.js";
```

## Fetching from a URL

### `getGeoJSON(target_url, responseFunction, tokenkey?, tokenvalue?)`

Fetches GeoJSON from `target_url`. The parameter order is the same as `getJSON` in [`api.js`](api/), and `responseFunction` is **always** called with `{ status, data }`:

| Event | `status` | `data` |
|---|---|---|
| Success, the content is GeoJSON | HTTP code (e.g. `200`) | `FeatureCollection` |
| The server responded, but the content is not GeoJSON | HTTP code (e.g. `200`, `404`) | `null` |
| Network failure, CORS rejected, or more than 15 seconds elapsed | `0` | `null` |

```javascript
import { getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geo.js";

getGeoJSON("https://github.com/petapedia/geojson/blob/main/contoh.geojson", (response) => {
    if (response.status === 0) {
        console.log("Request gagal: cek koneksi, atau server tidak mengizinkan CORS.");
        return;
    }
    if (!response.data) {
        console.log("Bukan GeoJSON, status:", response.status);
        return;
    }
    response.data.features.forEach((feature) => {
        console.log(feature.geometry.type, feature.properties.Gedung);
    });
    // Polygon Rektorat
    // Point ULBI
    // Polygon Auditorium
});
```

**GitHub file page links can be used directly.** An address of the form `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/<path>` (the one you copy from the address bar) actually responds with an HTML page, not the file contents. `getGeoJSON` automatically rewrites it to a `raw.githubusercontent.com` address before fetching the data.

**Why not `getJSON` from `api.js`?** `getJSON` always sends a `Content-Type` header, so the browser first sends a CORS *preflight*. Static file hosts such as `raw.githubusercontent.com` reject that preflight, so `getJSON` ends with `status: 0` even though the file exists. `getGeoJSON` sends no extra headers at all — unless you fill in `tokenkey` and `tokenvalue` — so static files can be fetched directly.

With a token (for your own backend):

```javascript
import { getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geo.js";
import { getCookie } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/cookie.js";

getGeoJSON("https://api.example.com/lokasi", tampilkan, "login", getCookie("login"));

function tampilkan(response) {
    console.log(response.status, response.data);
}
```

## Reading a local file

### `readGeoJSONFile(id, responseFunction)`

Reads the file the user picked in `<input type="file" id="...">`. The file is read directly in the browser and is not uploaded anywhere. `responseFunction` is called with a `FeatureCollection`, or `null` if no file has been picked yet, the file could not be read, or its content is not GeoJSON.

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<input id="berkas" type="file" accept=".geojson,.json">
<script type="module" src="index.js"></script>
```

```javascript
// index.js
import { readGeoJSONFile } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geo.js";
import { onChange } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";

onChange("berkas", () => {
    readGeoJSONFile("berkas", (data) => {
        if (!data) {
            console.log("File itu bukan GeoJSON.");
            return;
        }
        console.log(data.features.length, "fitur");
    });
});
```

## Parsing data you already have

### `parseGeoJSON(input)`

Use this when you already have the data in hand — for example text from a `<textarea>`, or an object from another API response. `input` may be JSON text or an object produced by `JSON.parse`. Returns a `FeatureCollection`, or `null` if `input` is not GeoJSON. `getGeoJSON` and `readGeoJSONFile` use this function internally.

Accepted input shapes:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `FeatureCollection` | The same `FeatureCollection` (other members such as `name` are preserved) |
| A single `Feature` | A `FeatureCollection` containing that one feature |
| A single bare geometry (`Point`, `LineString`, `Polygon`, `Multi*`, `GeometryCollection`) | A `FeatureCollection` containing one feature with `properties: {}` |
| An array of `Feature`s/geometries (the shape backends typically return from a MongoDB query) | A `FeatureCollection` containing all of them |

```javascript
import { parseGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geo.js";

parseGeoJSON('{"type":"Point","coordinates":[107.575914,-6.8732098]}');
// { type: "FeatureCollection", features: [
//     { type: "Feature", properties: {}, geometry: { type: "Point", coordinates: [107.575914, -6.8732098] } }
// ] }

parseGeoJSON('{"error":"not found"}'); // null
parseGeoJSON("bukan json");            // null
```

What is guaranteed about the result:

- `feature.properties` is always an object. `properties: null` (valid in GeoJSON) is turned into `{}`, so `feature.properties.nama` never throws.
- `feature.geometry` can be `null` — GeoJSON allows features without a location. Check it before reading `feature.geometry.type`.
- Every geometry has a known `type` and `coordinates` containing numbers, with the array depth matching its type.
- The input object is not modified; the result is a new object.

Invalid items inside a `FeatureCollection` or array (for example coordinates given as the text `"107.5"` instead of a number) are **skipped**; they do not make the whole dataset fail. The indexes of skipped items are written to the console.

## Reading the data's contents

All the functions below accept the same input shapes as `parseGeoJSON` — the result of `getGeoJSON`, a single `Feature`, or a single geometry. The examples use `data` from [contoh.geojson](https://github.com/petapedia/geojson/blob/main/contoh.geojson).

### `getBBox(geojson)`

The bounding box of all the data: `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]`. Returns `null` if the data has no coordinates at all.

```javascript
getBBox(data); // [107.5755063, -6.8739195, 107.5762898, -6.8732098]
```

### `getCenter(geojson)`

The center point of the bounding box as `[lng, lat]`, or `null` if the data has no coordinates. Handy for centering a map. This is the center of the box, not the *centroid* (center of mass) of the geometry.

```javascript
getCenter(data); // [107.57589805, -6.8735646500000005]
```

### `getPropertyKeys(geojson)`

The property names used by the features in the data, without duplicates, in order of first appearance. Useful for building a table header when not every feature has the same properties.

```javascript
getPropertyKeys(data); // ["Gedung", "Kampus"]
```

### `getCoordinates(geojson)`

Every position in the data, flattened into a single `[[lng, lat], ...]` array, regardless of geometry type.

```javascript
getCoordinates(data).length; // 11
```

### `toLatLng(position)`

Flips a single `[lng, lat]` position into `[lat, lng]`.

```javascript
toLatLng([107.575914, -6.8732098]); // [-6.8732098, 107.575914]
```

## Example: showing it on a map

To draw the data on a map, use [`map.js`](map) — CrootJS's own map module, with no external library. All `geo.js` functions are also exported from `map.js`, so a single import is enough:

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, fitMap, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";

createMap("peta"); // the <div id="peta"> element must get a height from CSS

getGeoJSON("https://github.com/petapedia/geojson/blob/main/contoh.geojson", (response) => {
    if (!response.data) return;
    addGeoJSON("peta", response.data);
    fitMap("peta", response.data);
});
```

Full example (URL, local file, map, and property table): [demo](https://croot.js.org/examples/geo/geojson/) · [source](https://github.com/crootjs/examples/tree/main/geo/geojson).

## Notes

- **GeoJSON coordinate order is `[longitude, latitude]`** — the reverse of what people usually write ("lat, long"). [`map.js`](map) uses the same order, so coordinates from the data can be used directly. Leaflet and Google Maps expect `[lat, lng]`; if you use either of them, flip the coordinates first with `toLatLng()`.
- `getGeoJSON` is subject to CORS. The server hosting the file must send the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header; otherwise the result is `status: 0`. GitHub (`raw.githubusercontent.com`), GitHub Pages, and jsDelivr send it.
- Validation only checks the shape of the data (geometry type and `coordinates` structure). This module does not check whether polygon rings are closed, or whether coordinate values make sense (for example a latitude outside -90..90).
- `getBBox` computes the minimum and maximum values as they are, so data crossing the 180° meridian (the antimeridian) produces a box that stretches around the world.
- To compute things from the data — distance, area, point in area, nearest point — see [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure); for routes along its lines, [`georoute.js`](georoute).
- Data shown on the page comes from outside. Set property values with `textContent`/`setInnerText`, not `innerHTML`/`setInner`, so the content is not executed as HTML.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/map

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../map)*

# `map.js` Module Documentation

`map.js` displays an interactive map and draws GeoJSON data on top of it — written from scratch, without Leaflet or any other map library. The basemap is made of raster tiles (default: OpenStreetMap), the data is drawn as SVG, and everything can be panned, zoomed, and clicked, with either a mouse or a finger.

Its CSS is *injected* automatically by the module itself (like [`toast.js`](toast)), so there is no CSS file to link. The browser downloads about 13 KB (gzip): `map.min.js` plus the [`geo.js`](geo) it uses. For comparison, Leaflet is about 46 KB (gzip) for its JS and CSS.

Icon markers, a scale bar, "my location", live tracking, coordinates, a right-click menu, fullscreen, drawing and editing geometry, address search, offline maps, 3D models on the map, measuring tools, image overlays, PNG export, point clustering, heatmaps, and routing live in separate [add-on modules](#add-on-modules), 1–8 KB each, so a page only downloads what it uses.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, fitMap, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
```

All [`geo.js`](geo) functions (`getGeoJSON`, `readGeoJSONFile`, `parseGeoJSON`, `getBBox`, and others) are re-exported from `map.js` as well. A page that shows a map only needs to import from `map.js`.

## Minimal Example

The map's container element **must have a height** set in CSS. The map fills that element completely; an element with no height means a map 0 pixels tall (the module logs a warning to the console when that happens).

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
<div id="peta" class="peta"></div>
<script type="module" src="index.js"></script>
```

```css
/* style.css */
.peta {
    height: 360px;
}
```

```javascript
// index.js
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, fitMap, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";

createMap("peta");

getGeoJSON("https://github.com/petapedia/geojson/blob/main/contoh.geojson", (response) => {
    if (!response.data) {
        console.log("gagal membaca GeoJSON, status:", response.status);
        return;
    }
    addGeoJSON("peta", response.data); // draw the data
    fitMap("peta", response.data);     // fit the view to the data
});
```

The result: a map with two building polygons and one point; click one of them to see its `properties` in a popup.

Every `map.js` function takes an **element ID** as its first parameter, just like the [`element.js`](element/) functions. There is no map object to keep around.

## `createMap(id, options)`

Creates a map inside the element with ID `id`. Calling it again for the same ID replaces the old map.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `center` | `[118, -2.5]` (Indonesia) | View center, `[lng, lat]` |
| `zoom` | `4` | Initial zoom level |
| `minZoom` | `1` | Farthest zoom allowed |
| `maxZoom` | `19` | Closest zoom allowed |
| `tiles` | OpenStreetMap tiles | Raster tile URL pattern with `{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}` — see [URL patterns](#tile-url-patterns). `false` = no basemap |
| `attribution` | — | Attribution for your own `tiles`: text, a DOM element (for links), or an array of them when there is more than one source |
| `attributionPrefix` | `true` | `false` = no "CrootJS" link in front of the attribution |
| `maxNativeZoom` | same as `maxZoom` | Highest tile level available on the server. Above it, tiles from that level are scaled up (*overzoom*), so `maxZoom` can be higher |
| `labels` | — | URL pattern (or array of patterns) for transparent label tiles drawn on top of `tiles` — for satellite imagery + street names (*hybrid*) |
| `subdomains` | `"abc"` | Replacement for `{s}` in the URL pattern: a string or an array |
| `errorTiles` | — | URL of an image to show in place of tiles that fail to load |
| `zoomControl` | `true` | `false` = no + / − buttons |
| `scrollZoom` | `true` | `false` = the mouse wheel keeps scrolling the page instead of zooming the map |

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });
```

## `addGeoJSON(id, geojson, options)`

Draws GeoJSON on the map. `geojson` can be anything [`parseGeoJSON`](geo) accepts: a `FeatureCollection`, a single `Feature`, a bare geometry, an array of these, or JSON text. All geometry types are supported (`Point`, `LineString`, `Polygon`, their `Multi` versions, and `GeometryCollection`).

Returns a `remove()` function that removes that layer again — the same pattern as `dismiss()` in [`toast.js`](toast). That function also has `remove.show()`, `remove.hide()`, `remove.setStyle(style)`, and `remove.setOrder(order)` for layers that have no name (see [Named Layers](#named-layers)).

```javascript
const hapusGedung = addGeoJSON("peta", dataGedung);
// ...
hapusGedung.hide(); // hide temporarily
hapusGedung.show();
hapusGedung();      // only this layer disappears
```

`options` (all optional):

**`style`** — how features look. Either an object, or a function `(feature) => object` to style each feature differently:

| Key | Applies to | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `stroke` | lines, polygon outlines, point outlines | blue `#2563eb` (points: white) |
| `strokeWidth` | lines, polygon outlines, point outlines | lines 3, polygons 2, points 2 |
| `strokeOpacity` | lines, polygon outlines, point outlines | 1 |
| `fill` | polygons, points | blue `#2563eb` |
| `fillOpacity` | polygons, points | polygons 0.25, points 1 |
| `radius` | points | 7 (pixels) |
| `strokeDasharray` | lines, polygon outlines, point outlines | solid line. `"6 4"` or `[6, 4]` = 6 pixels of line, 4 pixels of gap |
| `lineCap` | line ends | `"round"` (others: `"butt"`, `"square"`) |
| `lineJoin` | line corners | `"round"` (others: `"miter"`, `"bevel"`) |

```javascript
// all features red
addGeoJSON("peta", data, { style: { stroke: "#dc2626", fill: "#dc2626" } });

// color depends on a property; null = use the default style
addGeoJSON("peta", data, {
    style: (feature) => feature.properties.Gedung === "Rektorat" ? { fill: "#16a34a", stroke: "#16a34a" } : null,
});
```

Line widths, dash lengths, and point sizes stay the same on screen at any zoom level.

```javascript
// indicative route: dashed line
addGeoJSON("peta", jalurRencana, { style: { stroke: "#ea580c", strokeDasharray: [8, 6], lineCap: "butt" } });
```

**`popup`** — popup content when a feature is clicked:

| Value | Result |
|---|---|
| not set | a list of `name: value` from that feature's `properties` (features with no properties get no popup) |
| function `(feature) => text` | that text, shown as-is |
| function `(feature) => DOM element` | that element |
| function returning `null` | no popup for that feature |
| `false` | no popups at all |

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", data, { popup: (feature) => "Gedung " + feature.properties.Gedung });
```

Popup text is inserted as text, **not HTML** — tags inside the data or in the text you return are shown as-is and never executed. If you need links or formatting, return a DOM element:

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", data, {
    popup: (feature) => {
        const link = document.createElement("a");
        link.href = "/gedung?nama=" + encodeURIComponent(feature.properties.Gedung);
        link.textContent = "Detail " + feature.properties.Gedung;
        return link;
    },
});
```

**`hoverStyle`** and **`tooltip`** — feedback while the mouse cursor is over a feature (touch screens have no *hover*, so neither appears there):

- `hoverStyle` — a style object (same keys as `style`) applied on top while the cursor is over that feature.
- `tooltip` — a function `(feature) => text or DOM element` (or `null`); the result is shown in a small box that follows the cursor. The click popup still works as usual.

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", zona, {
    hoverStyle: { stroke: "#dc2626", strokeWidth: 4 },
    tooltip: (feature) => "Zona " + feature.properties.nomor,
});
```

**`label`** — text always shown on a feature: a property name, or a function `(feature) => text` (`null` = no label). A point's label sits at the point, a line's label at the middle of its length, and a polygon's label at its centroid. Labels that collide with other labels are hidden, then reappear when the map is zoomed and there is enough room — layers on top take priority, then the order of features in the data.

`labelOptions` (optional): `minZoom` / `maxZoom` (labels only show within this zoom range), `className` (an extra CSS class for the label element), `overlap: true` (no collision avoidance).

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", kontur, {
    label: (feature) => feature.properties.elevasi + " m",
    labelOptions: { minZoom: 16, className: "label-kontur" },
});
```

**`name`, `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, `order`, `visible`, `attribution`** — see [Named Layers](#named-layers).

**`renderer`** and **`simplify`** — see [Large Data](#large-data-canvas-and-simplification).

## Large Data: Canvas and Simplification

By default every shape is drawn as its own SVG element. That works well up to a few thousand shapes, but it starts to get heavy on phones once there are thousands of lines. Two `addGeoJSON` options for data like that:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `renderer` | `"svg"` | `"canvas"` = the whole layer is drawn on a single `<canvas>`, with no element per shape. Styles (including dashes), popups, `hoverStyle`, `tooltip`, labels, and `onMapClick` still work — clicks and *hover* are computed from the geometry itself |
| `simplify` | `0` | Simplification tolerance in screen pixels, e.g. `1`. Per zoom level, points that deviate less than that from a straight line are dropped (Douglas-Peucker), so when zoomed far out a line with thousands of points can be drawn with just dozens. Applies to both SVG and canvas |

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", jaringanFiber, {    // e.g. 5,600 lines
    name: "fiber",
    renderer: "canvas",
    simplify: 1,
    style: { stroke: "#ea580c", strokeWidth: 2 },
    tooltip: (feature) => feature.properties.kode,
});
```

Canvas layers are always **below** all SVG layers, whatever their `order` (`order` still controls the order among canvas layers). So large background layers suit canvas, while small layers that must appear on top stay in SVG.

## Named Layers

A layer given a `name` in `addGeoJSON` can be managed without redrawing it:

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `showLayer(id, name)` / `hideLayer(id, name)` | Shows / hides the layer. Its popup and *hover* are closed too when it is hidden |
| `setLayerStyle(id, name, style)` | Replaces the style of the whole layer; `style` is an object or a function, just like in `addGeoJSON` |
| `setLayerOrder(id, name, order)` | Stacking order: higher is on top |
| `removeLayer(id, name)` | Removes the layer |
| `getLayers(id)` | List of named layers from bottom to top: `[{ name, visible, order }]` |

Related `addGeoJSON` options:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | — | Layer name. A new layer with a name already in use **replaces** that old layer — an easy way to update data |
| `minZoom`, `maxZoom` | all zooms | The layer only shows within this zoom range, e.g. a block plan that is only useful at zoom 18 and above |
| `order` | `0` | Stacking order. Layers with the same `order` are stacked in the order they were added |
| `visible` | `true` | `false` = added in a hidden state |
| `attribution` | — | This layer's data source; added to the map attribution for as long as the layer exists |

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", batasZona, { name: "zona", order: 1, style: { strokeDasharray: "4 4" } });
addGeoJSON("peta", denahBlok, { name: "blok", minZoom: 18 });

hideLayer("peta", "zona");
setLayerStyle("peta", "blok", (feature) => ({ fill: feature.properties.terisi ? "#16a34a" : "#9ca3af" }));
```

For a ready-made checkbox list, see `addLayerControl` in [`mapcontrol.js`](mapcontrol).

## `setTiles(id, tiles, options)`

Replaces the basemap **without recreating the map**: layers, markers, an open popup, and the view all stay where they are. The old basemap tiles are kept until the new tiles finish loading, so the map does not flash blank.

`tiles` is the same as the `tiles` option of `createMap` (no value = OpenStreetMap, `false` = no basemap). `options` takes `labels`, `maxNativeZoom`, `subdomains`, `errorTiles`, and `attribution`, the same as in `createMap`; any not given revert to their defaults. `minZoom` and `maxZoom` may also be given — for example for a basemap that must not be zoomed past level 17 — but unlike the other options, those not given **stay** as they were (see `setZoomRange` below).

```javascript
// switch to satellite imagery + labels (hybrid)
setTiles("peta", "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}", {
    labels: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
    maxNativeZoom: 18,
    attribution: "Tiles © Esri",
});

setTiles("peta"); // back to OpenStreetMap
```

For a ready-made basemap picker, see `addBasemapControl` in [`mapcontrol.js`](mapcontrol).

## `setZoomRange(id, minZoom, maxZoom)`

Changes the allowed zoom range without recreating the map. A `minZoom` or `maxZoom` that is not given (`undefined`/`null`) is left unchanged. If the current zoom is outside the new range, the map is immediately zoomed to the nearest limit, and the + / − buttons adjust accordingly.

```javascript
setZoomRange("peta", null, 17); // no closer than zoom 17
setZoomRange("peta", 10);       // no farther than zoom 10, upper limit unchanged
```

## `fitMap(id, geojson, padding = 24)`

Fits the view to all of the data. `geojson` is as flexible as in `addGeoJSON`, or can be a bounding box `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` directly. `padding` is the empty space (in pixels) between the data and the map edge — one number for all sides, or per side `{ top, right, bottom, left }` (sides not given stay at 24), for example so the data is not covered by a panel.

```javascript
fitMap("peta", data);
fitMap("peta", [95, -11, 141, 6]);         // all of Indonesia
fitMap("peta", data, { left: 320 });       // a 300-pixel-wide panel on the left of the map
```

Per-side padding also suits a responsive "zoom to" button — panel on the left on wide screens, at the bottom on phones:

```javascript
const sempit = window.matchMedia("(max-width: 640px)").matches;
fitMap("peta", getBBox(dataLokasi), sempit ? { bottom: 260 } : { left: 340 });
```

- Data consisting of a single point is shown at zoom 17.
- Data without coordinates (or that is not GeoJSON) does not change the view.
- With a basemap, the zoom is rounded down to a whole level so tile images stay sharp, so the data may look smaller than the available space. With `tiles: false` the data is fitted exactly.
- A map whose element is still `display: none` has no size yet, so it cannot be fitted. Call `fitMap` after the element is shown.

## `setMapView(id, center, zoom)` and `getMapView(id)`

`setMapView` moves the view to `center` (`[lng, lat]`). `zoom` is optional; if not given, the current zoom level is kept.

`getMapView` returns the current view: `{ center: [lng, lat], zoom }`.

```javascript
setMapView("peta", [106.8272, -6.1754], 12); // Jakarta
setMapView("peta", [107.6191, -6.9175]);     // move to Bandung, zoom stays at 12

getMapView("peta"); // { center: [107.6191, -6.917499999999983], zoom: 12 }
```

The returned `center` may differ from what you passed in the last few digits (floating-point rounding during projection); the difference is far below one millimeter on the ground.

`zoom` is always clamped to `minZoom`..`maxZoom`. While a gesture (mouse wheel, pinch) is in progress, `zoom` can be fractional.

## `onMapClick(id, runFunction)`

`runFunction(position, feature)` is called every time the map is clicked or *tapped* (panning the map does not count as a click):

- `position` — `[lng, lat]` of the clicked point.
- `feature` — the GeoJSON feature that was clicked, or `null` if the basemap was clicked.

The most common use: picking a location for a form.

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, onMapClick } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { setValue } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });

let hapusPenanda = () => {};
onMapClick("peta", (position) => {
    setValue("longitude", position[0]);
    setValue("latitude", position[1]);

    // the old marker is replaced by a new one at the clicked point
    hapusPenanda();
    hapusPenanda = addGeoJSON("peta", { type: "Point", coordinates: position });
});
```

## `onMapContextMenu(id, runFunction)`

`runFunction(position, feature, detail)` is called when the map is **right-clicked**, **long-pressed** on a touch screen (about 0.5 seconds without moving the finger), or when the **Menu**/**Shift+F10** key is pressed while the map has focus:

- `position` — `[lng, lat]` of the point. From the keyboard: the map center.
- `feature` — the GeoJSON feature at that point, or `null`.
- `detail` — `{ point, keyboard }`: `point` = `[x, y]` in pixels from the map's top-left corner; `keyboard` = `true` if opened from the keyboard.

While there is a listener, the browser's built-in menu does not appear on the map, except inside popups and controls. Returns a `stop()` function; once the last listener stops, the browser's built-in menu appears again.

For a ready-made menu complete with submenus, keyboard support, and a dark theme, use [`addContextMenu`](mapcontrol#addcontextmenuid-items-options) from `mapcontrol.js`. `onMapContextMenu` is for your own UI:

```javascript
import { createMap, onMapContextMenu, showPopup } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 14 });
onMapContextMenu("peta", (position) => {
    showPopup("peta", position, `${position[1].toFixed(5)}, ${position[0].toFixed(5)}`);
});
```

## `onMapMove(id, runFunction)` and `getMapBounds(id)`

`runFunction({ center, zoom })` is called every time the view changes: panned, zoomed, or when the map's size changes. While a gesture is in progress it is called on every frame. Returns a `stop()` function to stop listening.

`getMapBounds(id)` returns the part of the world currently visible as a bounding box `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]`.

The two are commonly used together to request **only the data in the visible area** from a backend. Because `onMapMove` fires very often, wrap it with [`debounce`](debounce) so a request is sent only after the map stops moving:

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, clearMap, onMapMove, getMapBounds, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { debounce } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/debounce.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 16 });

onMapMove("peta", debounce(() => {
    const bbox = getMapBounds("peta");
    getGeoJSON("https://api.example.com/lokasi?bbox=" + bbox.join(","), (response) => {
        if (!response.data) return;
        clearMap("peta");
        addGeoJSON("peta", response.data);
    });
}, 400));
```

## `mapToPoint(id, position)` and `pointToPosition(id, point)`

Converts a `[lng, lat]` position into an `[x, y]` point in pixels (measured from the map's top-left corner), and back. The result of `mapToPoint` can lie outside the map's size if the position is not currently visible.

```javascript
mapToPoint("peta", [107.575914, -6.8732098]); // e.g. [412.6, 180.3]
pointToPosition("peta", [0, 0]);              // [lng, lat] at the map's top-left corner
```

Together with `onMapMove`, these two functions are enough to build your own HTML elements that follow the map. For markers, use [`mapmarker.js`](mapmarker), which already takes care of that.

## `addMapControl(id, element, corner = "top-right")`

Places an element you made — a button, a legend, an info box — in a corner of the map: `"top-left"`, `"top-right"`, `"bottom-left"`, or `"bottom-right"`. Several controls in the same corner are stacked neatly, and clicks inside them do not pan or click the map. Returns a `remove()` function.

```javascript
const legenda = document.createElement("div");
legenda.className = "legenda"; // its look comes from your page's CSS
legenda.textContent = "Biru: gedung kampus";
addMapControl("peta", legenda, "bottom-right");
```

## `showPopup(id, position, content)` and `closePopup(id)`

Shows a popup at `position` (`[lng, lat]`) without needing a feature there. `content` is text (shown as-is, not HTML) or a DOM element. There is only one popup per map; a new popup replaces the old one.

```javascript
showPopup("peta", [107.575914, -6.8732098], "Kampus ULBI");
closePopup("peta");
```

If the popup is cut off by the map edge, the map is panned slightly so the popup is fully visible. This only applies when the `position` is currently visible; `showPopup` at a faraway place does not make the map jump there (use `setMapView` first).

## `clearMap(id)` and `removeMap(id)`

- `clearMap(id)` removes all GeoJSON layers and closes the popup. The basemap stays. Use it before drawing new data to replace old data.
- `removeMap(id)` removes the map from the element and stops all of its listeners. The element itself remains and can be used by `createMap` again.

## Built-in Interactions

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Drag with the mouse or one finger | pans the map |
| Mouse wheel / trackpad pinch | zooms at the cursor position |
| Two-finger pinch | zooms between the two fingers |
| Double-click | zooms in one level at the cursor position |
| Right-click / one-finger long press / Menu key | `onMapContextMenu` and `addContextMenu`, if used; otherwise, the browser's built-in menu |
| + / − buttons | zooms one level at the map center |
| Arrow keys (while the map has focus) | pans the map |
| `+` / `-` keys (while the map has focus) | zoom |
| Click / tap a feature | opens its popup |
| Cursor over a feature (mouse) | `hoverStyle` and `tooltip`, if the layer uses them |

Users who have enabled *reduce motion* on their system get zooming without animation.

## Basemaps

**OpenStreetMap (default).** Tiles are fetched from `tile.openstreetmap.org`, and the attribution "CrootJS | © OpenStreetMap contributors" is automatically shown in the bottom-right corner — the data license requires it, so do not hide it. The OpenStreetMap tile servers are free but run by volunteers and have a [usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/): fine for learning and low-traffic sites. For high-traffic applications, use your own tile provider.

**Other tile providers.** Set `tiles` to their URL pattern and `attribution` to the attribution text the provider requires:

```javascript
createMap("peta", {
    tiles: "https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
    attribution: "© Example Maps",
});
```

**Custom tile sources.** Besides a URL pattern, `tiles` (and the entries of `labels`) can be an object `{ getTile(z, x, y) }` that returns a Promise of an image `Blob`, a URL, or `null` if that tile does not exist. This is how [`mapoffline.js`](mapoffline) displays a map from a single PMTiles file, including from a file on the device with no internet:

```javascript
import { openPMTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapoffline.js";

const arsip = await openPMTiles("peta-bandung.pmtiles");
createMap("peta", { tiles: arsip, maxNativeZoom: arsip.maxZoom, center: arsip.center, zoom: 13 });
```

The attribution always starts with a "CrootJS" link to this site, then the basemap source, then each data layer's `attribution` — identical sources are written only once. Its content is updated every time the basemap is replaced or a layer is added/removed. `attributionPrefix: false` in `createMap` removes the "CrootJS" link; the tile provider's attribution is still shown.

### Tile URL Patterns

| Placeholder | Replaced with |
|---|---|
| `{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}` | the tile's zoom level, column, and row |
| `{-y}` | the tile row in the TMS scheme (counted from the bottom), for servers such as GeoServer/TileCache |
| `{s}` | a subdomain, rotating through `subdomains` (default `"abc"`) to spread the load |
| `{r}` | `@2x` on retina screens, empty on regular screens |

```javascript
createMap("peta", {
    tiles: "https://{s}.tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}{r}.png",
    subdomains: "abcd",
    errorTiles: "/img/tile-kosong.png", // replacement for tiles that fail to load
    attribution: "© Example Maps",
});
```

### Satellite Imagery, Overzoom, and Hybrid

Many imagery providers only have tiles up to zoom 18 over most areas. `maxNativeZoom: 18` lets the map still zoom up to `maxZoom` — level-18 tiles are scaled up instead of left blank. `labels` stacks transparent label tiles (street and place names) on top of the imagery:

```javascript
createMap("peta", {
    maxZoom: 21,
    maxNativeZoom: 18,
    tiles: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
    labels: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
    attribution: "Tiles © Esri",
});
```

**No basemap.** With `tiles: false` only your data is drawn, on a plain background — no requests to a tile server at all:

```javascript
createMap("peta", { tiles: false });
```

## Add-on Modules

Features that not every map needs are split into their own modules. Import only the ones you use:

| Module | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`mapmarker.js`](mapmarker) | Pin markers, image icons, or your own elements — with labels, popups, and dragging (`addMarker`) |
| [`mapcontrol.js`](mapcontrol) | Scale bar, "my location", live tracking, basemap picker (list or image cards), layer checkbox list, cursor coordinates, right-click menu, and fullscreen (`addScaleBar`, `addLocateButton`, `locateUser`, `addTrackButton`, `trackUser`, `addBasemapControl`, `setBasemap`, `addLayerControl`, `addCoordinateControl`, `addContextMenu`, `addFullscreenButton`) |
| [`maptools.js`](maptools) | Distance and area measuring tool, georeferenced images with rotation, exporting the view to PNG (`addMeasureControl`, `measure`, `addImageOverlay`, `exportMapImage`, `downloadMapImage`) |
| [`mapcluster.js`](mapcluster) | Point clustering for very large point datasets (`addCluster`) |
| [`mapsearch.js`](mapsearch) | Find places by name/address and addresses by point (Nominatim/OSM or your own provider), plus an on-map search box (`searchPlace`, `reverseGeocode`, `addSearchControl`) |
| [`mapoffline.js`](mapoffline) | Basemap from a single raster PMTiles file — from a server, or from a file on the device with no internet (`openPMTiles`) |
| [`mapmodel.js`](mapmodel) | glTF/GLB 3D models at their location on the map, sized in meters (`addModel`) |
| [`mapdraw.js`](mapdraw) | Drawing and editing points, lines, and polygons; the result is GeoJSON (`addDrawControl`, `startDrawing`, `editFeature`) |
| [`mapheat.js`](mapheat) | Point-density heatmaps, and square/hexagon grid maps colored by value such as signal coverage maps (`addHeatmap`, `addGridMap`) |
| [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure) | Distance, length, area, point-in-area, nearest point, radius circles |
| [`georoute.js`](georoute) | Shortest route along the lines in GeoJSON data (`findRoute`) |

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addMarker } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapmarker.js";
import { addScaleBar, addLocateButton } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcontrol.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });
addMarker("peta", [107.575914, -6.8732098], { label: "ULBI", popup: "Kampus ULBI" });
addScaleBar("peta");
addLocateButton("peta");
```

## Writing Your Own Add-on

`createMap` attaches a small interface to the map element, in the `crootjsMap` property. That is how `mapmarker.js` and `mapcontrol.js` work, and your own module can use the same route:

```javascript
// penanda.js - a simple add-on module: a piece of text pinned to one position
export function addText(id, position, text) {
    const map = document.getElementById(id).crootjsMap; // undefined if the map has not been created yet

    const element = document.createElement("div");
    element.className = "penanda"; // needs position: absolute from your CSS
    element.textContent = text;
    map.overlay.appendChild(element);

    const place = () => {
        const point = map.toPoint(position);
        element.style.transform = `translate(${point[0]}px, ${point[1]}px)`;
    };
    place();
    map.onMove(place); // called every time the map moves
}
```

| `crootjsMap` member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `overlay` | Element to put your HTML elements in: above the data, below the popup, clipped at the map edge |
| `toPoint(position)` / `toPosition(point)` | `[lng, lat]` to pixels and back |
| `getView()` | `{ center, zoom }` |
| `setView(center, zoom)` | Moves the view |
| `panBy(dx, dy)` | Pans the map by a number of pixels |
| `onMove(runFunction)` | Listens for view changes; returns `stop()` |
| `onTap(element, runFunction)` | Handles taps on an element in `overlay`: the map does not treat them as map clicks (`onMapClick` is not called), while drags that start on that element still pan the map |
| `addControl(element, corner)` | Places an element in a corner of the map; returns `remove()` |
| `showPopup(position, content, offset)` / `closePopup()` | Popup; `offset` = upward distance from the position, in pixels |
| `setTiles(tiles, options)` | Same as `setTiles(id, ...)` |
| `getLayers()` / `setLayerVisible(name, visible)` | List of named layers; shows/hides one layer |
| `setZoomRange(minZoom, maxZoom)` | Same as `setZoomRange(id, ...)` |
| `root` | The map element itself (containing all layers) — e.g. for listening to `pointermove` |
| `underlay` | Element for images above the basemap and below the data (used by `addImageOverlay`) |
| `onClick(runFunction)` | Same as `onMapClick`; returns `stop()` |
| `onContextMenu(runFunction)` | Same as `onMapContextMenu`; returns `stop()` |
| `captureClick(runFunction)` | Borrows map clicks: while active, clicks and double-clicks are only passed to `runFunction(position, "click" \| "dblclick")` — no popups, no double-click zoom, no `onMapClick`. Returns `release()`. Used by the measuring tool |

**Add-on modules must not import `map.js`.** A page usually loads `map.min.js`, whereas `import "./map.js"` from another module loads a *second copy* with its own list of maps — and the maps created by the page will not be found. The interface on the element avoids that: your module works with whichever copy of `map.js` the page uses.

## Notes

- **All positions use GeoJSON order: `[longitude, latitude]`** — `center`, `position` in `onMapClick`, `showPopup`, and `getMapView`. So coordinates from GeoJSON data can be used directly without swapping.
- Within a layer, points are always drawn on top, regardless of their order in the data, so they are not covered by polygons. Layers added later sit above earlier layers, unless set otherwise with `order`.
- Thin lines have an invisible click area 20 pixels wide. A dense line layer (e.g. contours) on top of polygons can block clicks and *hover* on those polygons; put the line layer underneath with `order`.
- The map adjusts itself when its element's size changes, including when an element that was `display: none` (e.g. tab content) is shown.
- The map's default styles (buttons, popups, labels, markers) are *injected* as a `<style>` at the **start** of `<head>`, so your page's CSS overrides them without `!important` — for example `.crootjs-marker-label { color: #fff; text-shadow: 0 0 3px #000; }` for white marker labels over satellite imagery.
- A page can have several maps, each with its own element ID.
- Functions called with an ID that has not been passed to `createMap` do not throw an error; they log a warning to the console and do nothing.

### Limitations

- The projection is Web Mercator only (the one used by almost all web maps), with latitude limited to ±85.05°.
- Basemaps are raster (image) tiles only. Vector tiles are not supported.
- The map does not wrap around left-right past the 180° meridian.
- Data is drawn as SVG, one element per shape, except for `renderer: "canvas"` layers. SVG works well for hundreds up to a few thousand features; for thousands of lines use canvas (see [Large Data](#large-data-canvas-and-simplification)), and for tens of thousands of points use [`mapcluster.js`](mapcluster), which clusters them.
- Feature labels are written horizontally; line labels do not follow the direction of the line.
- Drawing and editing shapes directly on the map is in the [`mapdraw.js`](mapdraw) add-on.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapmarker

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapmarker)*

# `mapmarker.js` Module Documentation

`mapmarker.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map): markers shaped as a pin, an image icon, or your own HTML element — with a label, a popup, and optional dragging. This module is separate from `map.js` so pages that don't need markers don't have to download it (about 2 KB gzip).

Points in GeoJSON data are already drawn by `addGeoJSON` as small circles. `addMarker` is for when you need more than that: a prominent pin, your own icon, a name label, or a marker the user drags to pick a location.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addMarker } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapmarker.js";
```

The map must be created with `createMap` before `addMarker` is called.

## `addMarker(id, position, options)`

Places a marker at `position` (`[lng, lat]`) on the map with ID `id`. Without `options`, the result is a red pin.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });

addMarker("peta", [107.575914, -6.8732098]);
addMarker("peta", [107.5757, -6.8738], { label: "Rektorat", popup: "Gedung Rektorat" });
```

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `color` | Color of the default pin (any CSS value). Default: red |
| `icon` | Image URL to use instead of the pin |
| `size` | `[width, height]` of the `icon` image in pixels. Default: `[32, 32]` |
| `element` | Your own DOM element to use instead of the pin/icon |
| `anchor` | The part of the marker that sits on its position: `"bottom"` (default — bottom center, suits pins), `"center"` (suits round icons), `"top"`, `"left"`, `"right"`, `"top-left"`, `"top-right"`, `"bottom-left"`, or `"bottom-right"` |
| `offset` | `[dx, dy]` — additional shift in pixels from the anchor point (positive `dy` = downward). Default: `[0, 0]` |
| `label` | Text always shown below the marker |
| `title` | Tooltip text shown when the cursor is over the marker |
| `popup` | Text or DOM element shown when the marker is clicked |
| `onClick` | Function `(position)` called when the marker is clicked |
| `draggable` | `true` = the marker can be dragged with a mouse or finger |
| `onDragEnd` | Function `(position)` called after the marker has been dragged |

The return value is a controller object for that marker:

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `getPosition()` | The marker's current position, `[lng, lat]` |
| `setPosition(position)` | Moves the marker |
| `remove()` | Removes the marker from the map |

## Custom Icons and Elements

```javascript
// image icon, centered on its position
addMarker("peta", [107.5757, -6.8738], { icon: "kampus.png", size: [28, 28], anchor: "center" });

// your own element: its appearance comes entirely from your page's CSS
const lencana = document.createElement("span");
lencana.className = "lencana";
lencana.textContent = "12";
addMarker("peta", [107.5762, -6.8734], { element: lencana, anchor: "center" });
```

## Anchor and Offset

`anchor` determines which part of the marker sits exactly on its position, and `offset` shifts it slightly from there. For example, a pole number label placed to the right of its point, 6 pixels away:

```javascript
const nomor = document.createElement("span");
nomor.className = "nomor-tiang"; // its appearance comes from your page's CSS
nomor.textContent = "T-12";
addMarker("peta", [107.5757, -6.8738], { element: nomor, anchor: "left", offset: [6, 0] });
```

A marker's popup always appears above the marker's top edge, whatever its anchor.

## Draggable Markers

The most common use: the user drags the pin to the exact location, and its coordinates go into a form.

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addMarker } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapmarker.js";
import { setValue } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });

addMarker("peta", [107.5759, -6.8736], {
    draggable: true,
    title: "Geser ke lokasi yang tepat",
    onDragEnd: (position) => {
        setValue("longitude", position[0]);
        setValue("latitude", position[1]);
    },
});
```

To move a marker from code — for example to the point clicked on the map — use `setPosition`:

```javascript
import { onMapClick } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";

const pin = addMarker("peta", [107.5759, -6.8736]);
onMapClick("peta", (position) => pin.setPosition(position));
```

## Behavior

- **A click on a marker belongs to the marker.** The marker's `onClick` and `popup` run; the map's `onMapClick` is not called, and double-clicking a marker does not zoom the map.
- **Dragging a marker that is not `draggable` pans the map.** So a map full of markers stays easy to pan even when a finger lands on a marker.
- Markers move with the map as it pans and zooms, but their on-screen size stays the same.
- Markers with a `popup`, `onClick`, or `draggable` can be reached with the Tab key and activated with Enter.
- `popup` and `label` text is inserted as text, not HTML. For formatted content, pass a DOM element as `popup`.
- Markers disappear along with the map when it is removed (`removeMap`) or recreated (`createMap` with the same ID).

## Notes

- `clearMap` only removes GeoJSON layers; markers are not removed. Remove a marker with its own `remove()`.
- Each marker is one HTML element. For hundreds of markers this is comfortable; for thousands of points, draw them as GeoJSON data with `addGeoJSON` (lighter), and use markers only for the ones that need to stand out.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapcontrol

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapcontrol)*

# `mapcontrol.js` Module Documentation

`mapcontrol.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) containing the controls most often requested for a map: a **scale bar**, **my location**, **live tracking** (continuously following the location), a **basemap picker** (a list or picture cards), a **layer checklist**, **cursor coordinates**, a **right-click menu**, and **fullscreen**. It is kept separate from `map.js` so that pages that don't use it don't have to download it (about 8 KB gzipped).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addScaleBar, addLocateButton, locateUser, addTrackButton, trackUser, addBasemapControl, setBasemap, addLayerControl, addCoordinateControl, addContextMenu, addFullscreenButton } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcontrol.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addScaleBar(id, corner = "bottom-left")`

Shows a scale bar — for example "50 m" or "2 km" — that updates as the map is zoomed or panned. `corner` may be `"bottom-left"` (default), `"bottom-right"`, `"top-left"`, or `"top-right"`.

Returns a `remove()` function to take it off again.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });
addScaleBar("peta");
```

The bar length is computed for the latitude at the center of the map. In the Web Mercator projection the scale varies with latitude, so at the same zoom a "5 km" bar in Norway is as long on screen as a "10 km" bar at the equator.

## `addLocateButton(id, responseFunction, corner = "top-left")`

Adds a "my location" button to the map (default: below the zoom buttons). When clicked, the button runs `locateUser` below. `responseFunction` is optional and receives the same result.

Returns a `remove()` function to take the button off.

```javascript
addLocateButton("peta");
```

## `locateUser(id, responseFunction)`

Asks the browser for the device's location (once), then:

1. marks it on the map with a blue dot and an accuracy circle,
2. moves the view there — a map that is zoomed far out is brought in to zoom 16, a map that is already closer keeps its zoom,
3. calls `responseFunction` (optional) with the result.

| Event | What `responseFunction` receives |
|---|---|
| Location obtained | `{ position: [lng, lat], accuracy }` — `accuracy` in meters |
| Permission denied, device not supported, or 15 seconds elapsed | `null` |

```javascript
import { locateUser } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcontrol.js";
import { getDistance } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geomeasure.js";

const kampus = [107.575914, -6.8732098];

locateUser("peta", (lokasi) => {
    if (!lokasi) {
        console.log("Lokasi tidak didapat. Pastikan izin lokasi diberikan.");
        return;
    }
    const jarak = getDistance(lokasi.position, kampus);
    console.log(`Kamu ${Math.round(jarak)} m dari kampus (ketelitian ${Math.round(lokasi.accuracy)} m).`);
});
```

The circle around the blue dot shows the accuracy: the actual location is somewhere inside that circle. Its size is in meters, so it grows as the map is zoomed in; the blue dot itself stays the same size.

A map has only one location marker. Subsequent calls move the same marker.

## `trackUser(id, responseFunction, options)`

*Live tracking*: follows the device's location **continuously**. The difference from `locateUser`, which gets the location once: here the location marker on the map moves every time the browser reports a new position, until you stop it.

Returns a `stop()` function to stop tracking.

`responseFunction` (optional) is called on **every** update with:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `position` | `[lng, lat]` |
| `accuracy` | Accuracy, in meters |
| `speed` | Speed in meters per second, or `null` if the device does not report it |
| `heading` | Direction of travel in degrees from north, or `null` if the device does not report it |
| `timestamp` | Time of the reading, in milliseconds |

If location permission is denied or the device does not support it, `responseFunction` is called **once** with `null` and tracking stops on its own. Temporary disruptions such as a lost signal do not stop tracking; the browser retries.

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { trackUser } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcontrol.js";

createMap("peta");

// Travel trail: each new position is appended to a line that is redrawn.
const jejak = [];
let hapusJejak = () => {};

const stop = trackUser("peta", (lokasi) => {
    if (!lokasi) {
        console.log("Pelacakan tidak bisa dijalankan. Pastikan izin lokasi diberikan.");
        return;
    }
    jejak.push(lokasi.position);
    if (jejak.length > 1) {
        hapusJejak();
        hapusJejak = addGeoJSON("peta", { type: "LineString", coordinates: jejak }, { popup: false });
    }
});

// later, to stop:
// stop();
```

**The map pans along** so the location stays centered. The first update brings a map that is still zoomed far out in to zoom 16; after that, the user's chosen zoom is kept. As soon as the user pans the map themselves, the map stops following — the marker is still updated — so the map doesn't jump back while the user is looking at another place.

If the map must not move at all, turn this off with `options`:

```javascript
trackUser("peta", tampilkan, { follow: false });
```

## `addTrackButton(id, responseFunction, options, corner = "top-left")`

Adds a live tracking button to the map. The first click starts `trackUser`, the next click stops it; the button is blue while tracking is running. `responseFunction` and `options` are passed through to `trackUser`.

Returns a `remove()` function that stops tracking and takes the button off.

```javascript
addTrackButton("peta");
```

## `addBasemapControl(id, basemaps, options)`

Adds a basemap picker to the map. Choosing one calls [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options) — layers, markers, popups, and the view stay in place. There are two styles:

- **`"list"`** (default): a panel of radio buttons.
- **`"cards"`**: a single picture card showing the currently active basemap, like the Google Maps layer picker. Hovering over it (or clicking/tapping it) turns it into a grid of cards for all options; the active card has an accent-colored border.

`basemaps` is an array of `{ name, tiles, labels, maxNativeZoom, subdomains, errorTiles, attribution, minZoom, maxZoom, thumbnail }`; all keys except `name` and `thumbnail` are the same as the `setTiles` options. With `maxZoom`, each basemap can have its own zoom limit; the map is zoomed out immediately if it is currently closer than the selected basemap's limit.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `"list"` | `"list"` or `"cards"` |
| `selected` | `0` | Index or `name` of the basemap applied right away |
| `title` | `"Peta dasar"` | Title of the panel or grid (`""` = no title) |
| `corner` | `"top-right"` | Map corner. The card grid opens from the same corner |
| `onChange` | — | Function `(basemap)` called after the basemap is changed, including via `setBasemap` |
| `collapsed` | `false` | `"list"` only: `true` = the panel is tucked behind a layers icon button, opened and closed by clicking |
| `trigger` | automatic | `"cards"` only: `"hover"` (the grid opens on hover) or `"click"`. Defaults to `"hover"` on devices with a mouse and `"click"` on touch screens |
| `columns` | `3` | `"cards"` only: number of grid columns. On screens 640 px wide or less, at most 2 |
| `thumbnailCenter` | map center | `"cards"` only: the `[lng, lat]` point shown in the card images |
| `thumbnailZoom` | map zoom | `"cards"` only: zoom of the card images |

Returns a `remove()` function to take the control off; the last selected basemap stays applied.

```javascript
addBasemapControl("peta", [
    { name: "Jalan" }, // no tiles = OpenStreetMap
    {
        name: "Satelit",
        tiles: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
        maxNativeZoom: 18,
        attribution: "Tiles © Esri",
    },
    {
        name: "Hybrid",
        tiles: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
        labels: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
        maxNativeZoom: 18,
        attribution: "Tiles © Esri",
    },
]);
```

### Card style

```javascript
addBasemapControl("peta", basemaps, {
    style: "cards",
    thumbnailCenter: [125.8959, -9.014],
    thumbnailZoom: 14,
    selected: "Hybrid",
    onChange: (basemap) => console.log("Peta dasar:", basemap.name),
});
```

**Card images.** Set `thumbnail` to an image URL if you want your own image. Without `thumbnail`, the image is a single tile from that basemap itself: the tile containing `thumbnailCenter` at `thumbnailZoom`, using the same URL pattern as the map (`{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`, `{-y}`, `{s}`, `{r}`, and `maxNativeZoom` are respected). If the basemap has `labels`, the label tile is stacked on top of the base image — the Hybrid card shows the imagery along with its labels. `thumbnailCenter` and `thumbnailZoom` default to the map's center and zoom at the moment the control is added, so add the control after the map has been pointed at the work area, or set both.

**Opening and closing.** The grid closes when you click outside it, when Esc is pressed, after a card is chosen, or (with `"hover"`) when the cursor leaves it. With `"hover"`, the toggle card can still be clicked, so keyboard users can still open it.

**Accessibility.** The toggle card is a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`; each option card is a `<button aria-pressed>`. When the grid is opened by click or keyboard, focus moves to the active card; when it closes, focus returns to the toggle card.

**Styling.** Card colors follow `prefers-color-scheme` (light/dark). The accent color and card width can be changed via the CSS variables `--crootjs-map-accent` and `--crootjs-map-card-width`, and every class can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`:

```css
#peta {
    --crootjs-map-accent: #16a34a;     /* accent color */
    --crootjs-map-card-width: 104px;   /* card width, default 92px; the grid adjusts accordingly */
}
.crootjs-map-card-thumb { width: 84px; height: 84px; }   /* image size, default 72px */
```

The default width of 92 px fits a single-word name as long as "OpenStreetMap", even when bold on the active card. Longer names wrap to the next line between words; a word is only broken if it doesn't fit on a full line (with a hyphen in browsers that support `hyphens`).

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-map-cards` | Control wrapper |
| `.crootjs-map-cards-toggle` | Toggle card (active basemap) |
| `.crootjs-map-cards-grid` | Options grid |
| `.crootjs-map-cards-title` | Grid title |
| `.crootjs-map-card` | Each card, including the toggle card; the active one is `[aria-pressed="true"]` |
| `.crootjs-map-card-thumb`, `.crootjs-map-card-name` | Image and name inside the card |

## `setBasemap(id, name)`

Changes the basemap from code through the `addBasemapControl` picker most recently added to that map, so its radio button or card switches too and `onChange` is called as well. `name` is the basemap's `name` or index. Returns `true` on success, `false` if the map has no picker yet or no basemap with that name exists.

```javascript
setBasemap("peta", "Satelit");
```

To change the basemap without a picker, use [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options) from `map.js`.

## `addLayerControl(id, layers, options)`

Adds a checklist to show/hide named layers (the `name` option in [`addGeoJSON`](map#named-layers)). Checking a box only changes visibility — the layer is not redrawn, and popups open on other layers stay open.

`layers` is an array of names, or an array of `{ name, label }` if the text in the list differs from the name. `null` = all named layers that already exist when this function is called, from bottom to top.

`options` (all optional): `title` (default `"Lapisan"`), `corner` (default `"top-right"`), `collapsed`, and `onChange` — a function `(name, visible)` called every time a checkbox is changed.

Returns a `remove()` function to take the panel off.

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", jalurFiber, { name: "fiber" });
addGeoJSON("peta", batasZona, { name: "zona" });

addLayerControl("peta", [
    { name: "fiber", label: "Jalur fiber" },
    { name: "zona", label: "Batas zona" },
]);
```

## `addCoordinateControl(id, options)`

Shows the coordinates under the mouse cursor. Clicking (or tapping) the map **holds** the coordinates of that point and shows a copy button next to them. Touch screens have no cursor, so only the tapped coordinates are shown.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | `"lat, lng"` | Function `(position) => text` whose result is shown and copied. This is the hook for local coordinate systems |
| `precision` | `6` | Decimal places for the default format (6 ≈ 10 cm) |
| `corner` | `"bottom-left"` | Map corner |
| `onClick` | — | Function `(position, text)` called when coordinates are held |

Returns a `remove()` function.

The default format is ordered **lat, lng** (`-6.873600, 107.575900`) — the order accepted by the Google Maps search box and most GPS devices — even though `position` remains `[lng, lat]`.

The copy button uses the Clipboard API, which is only available on HTTPS pages (or `localhost`). On a plain `http://` page the text is selected instead, so just press Ctrl+C.

**Local grid (CAD).** With [`createAffineTransform`](geomeasure#createaffinetransformfrom-to) from `geomeasure.js`, coordinates can be shown in a project grid. For example, with three control points whose grid coordinates and lng/lat are known:

```javascript
import { createAffineTransform } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geomeasure.js";

const grid = [[1000, 2000], [1500, 2000], [1000, 2400]];                  // meters, CAD grid
const wgs84 = [[107.57520, -6.87410], [107.57974, -6.87407], [107.57517, -6.87048]];
const gridToWgs = createAffineTransform(grid, wgs84);

addCoordinateControl("peta", {
    format: (position) => {
        const [x, y] = gridToWgs.inverse(position);
        return `X ${x.toFixed(2)}  Y ${y.toFixed(2)}`;
    },
});
```

## `addContextMenu(id, items, options)`

A right-click menu on the map, like in Google Maps or QGIS. It appears when:

- the map is **right-clicked** with a mouse;
- the map is **long-pressed** on a touch screen (about 0.5 seconds without moving the finger) — including on iPhone, which has no right-click;
- the **Menu** key or **Shift+F10** is pressed while the map has focus. The menu appears in the center of the map and its first item is focused immediately.

While a context menu is active, the browser's built-in menu ("Save image", "Inspect", ...) does not appear on the map, except inside popups and controls, so their text can still be copied.

`items` may be an array of items, or a **function `(position, feature) => array of items`** that is called every time the menu opens:

- `position` — `[lng, lat]` of the right-clicked point.
- `feature` — the GeoJSON feature (`addGeoJSON`) at that point, or `null` if the basemap was clicked.

With a function, the menu contents can differ for empty map and for a feature. An empty array means the menu does not appear.

An item is an object:

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Item text |
| `onClick` | Function `(position, feature)` called when the item is chosen. The menu closes first |
| `icon` | Optional: short text or an emoji, an `<svg ...>` string, or a DOM element (e.g. a Lucide icon) |
| `disabled` | `true` = shown grayed out and cannot be chosen |
| `danger` | `true` = shown in red, for actions such as delete |
| `title` | Optional: *tooltip* text |
| `items` | Array of items: this item becomes a **submenu**. The submenu opens when the cursor hovers over it, when clicked, or with the right arrow key |

Besides objects, an item may also be:

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| `"-"` | Separator line. Separators at the start, at the end, or consecutive ones are removed automatically |
| `false`, `null`, `undefined` | Skipped, so a conditional item can simply be written `feature && { ... }` |
| `"coordinates"` | Shows the coordinates of that point (`lat, lng`); choosing it copies them to the clipboard |
| `"center"` | "Pusatkan di sini" (Center here) |
| `"zoom-in"` | "Perbesar di sini" (Zoom in here) — one level, centered on that point |
| `"zoom-out"` | "Perkecil" (Zoom out) — one level |

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `precision` | `6` | Decimal places for the `"coordinates"` item |
| `format` | `"lat, lng"` | Function `(position) => text` for the `"coordinates"` item, same as in `addCoordinateControl` |
| `onOpen` | — | Function `(position, feature)` called every time the menu opens |

Returns `{ close(), remove() }`. `remove()` removes the context menu, and the browser's built-in menu appears again.

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, setMapView } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addContextMenu } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcontrol.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 14 });
addGeoJSON("peta", dataBTS, { name: "bts" });

addContextMenu("peta", (position, feature) => [
    "coordinates",
    "center",
    "-",
    feature && { label: "Detail " + feature.properties.nama, onClick: () => bukaDetail(feature) },
    feature && { label: "Hapus BTS", danger: true, onClick: () => hapusBTS(feature) },
    "-",
    { label: "Tambah di sini", items: [
        { label: "Titik ukur", onClick: (position) => tambahTitikUkur(position) },
        { label: "BTS baru", onClick: (position) => tambahBTS(position) },
    ] },
    "zoom-in",
    "zoom-out",
]);
```

**`addGridMap` cells.** Heatmap cells are not GeoJSON features, so their `feature` is `null`. Get the cell with `cellAt(position)` from [`mapheat.js`](mapheat#addgridmapid-data-options):

```javascript
const cakupan = addGridMap("peta", hasilUkur, { value: "rsrp", shape: "hex", cellMeters: 100 });

addContextMenu("peta", (position, feature) => {
    const petak = feature ? null : cakupan.cellAt(position);
    return [
        "coordinates",
        petak && { label: `RSRP ${petak.value.toFixed(1)} dBm (${petak.count} titik)`, disabled: true },
        petak && { label: "Lihat pengukuran di petak ini", onClick: () => tampilkanPengukuran(petak) },
    ];
});
```

The menu closes when an item is chosen, when Esc or Tab is pressed, when the user clicks outside the menu, and when the map is panned or zoomed. Inside the menu, the up/down arrows, Home, and End move focus; Enter or Space chooses; the right/left arrows open/close a submenu. It flips to the left or upward if it doesn't fit on screen.

Only one context menu is open on a page at a time. If `addContextMenu` is called twice for the same map, both open a menu and the last one is what shows, so a single call with a function that builds all the items is enough.

Its appearance can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`. The dark theme follows `prefers-color-scheme`, and on touch screens the items are taller so they are easy to *tap*.

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-map-menu` | The menu box, and also each submenu (`role="menu"`, placed in `<body>`) |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-item` | Each item (`<button role="menuitem">`) |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-danger` | Items with `danger: true` |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-icon`, `.crootjs-map-menu-label`, `.crootjs-map-menu-arrow` | Icon, text, and the submenu `›` marker inside an item |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-separator` | Separator line |

For a menu of your own, use [`onMapContextMenu`](map#onmapcontextmenuid-runfunction) from `map.js`. That function gives you only the point, the feature, and its position, with no menu UI.

## `addFullscreenButton(id, corner = "top-left")`

Adds a fullscreen button: the map fills the whole screen; click again (or press Esc) to go back. Browsers without the Fullscreen API for elements — Safari on iPhone — get an emulation: the map fills the browser window. The map size adjusts itself in both directions.

Returns a `remove()` function, which also exits fullscreen.

```javascript
addFullscreenButton("peta");
```

## Notes

- **Location is only available on HTTPS pages** (or `localhost` during development). On a plain `http://` page the browser refuses without asking the user, and the result is `null`.
- The user must approve the browser's location permission request. If they have denied it before, the browser does not ask again until the permission is changed in the site settings.
- Accuracy depends on the device: a phone with GPS can be within a few meters, a laptop guessing from Wi-Fi can be off by hundreds of meters. Always check `accuracy` before using the position for decisions such as attendance.
- `locateUser` gets the location once; `trackUser` follows it continuously. Both use the same location marker.
- Continuous tracking drains the battery, especially with GPS. Stop it with `stop()` as soon as it is no longer needed.
- Tracking only runs while the page is open. Browsers slow down or stop location updates when the tab is in the background or the phone screen is off, so this is not for recording a trip with the screen off.
- How often new positions arrive is determined by the device and browser, not by this module.
- For your own controls (buttons, legends), use [`addMapControl`](map) from `map.js`.
- `addLayerControl` reads each checkbox's initial state from its layer. If a layer is hidden via `hideLayer` after the panel is created, its checkbox does not change.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/maptools

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../maptools)*

# `maptools.js` Module Documentation

`maptools.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) with tools for technical and survey maps: **distance and area measurement**, **georeferenced images** (for example a master plan or a scanned floor plan, which can be rotated), and **exporting the map view to PNG** for reports. It is kept separate from `map.js` so pages that don't use it don't have to download it (about 5 KB gzip, plus [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure) for the distance and area calculations).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addMeasureControl, measure, addImageOverlay, exportMapImage, downloadMapImage } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/maptools.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addMeasureControl(id, options)`

Adds two buttons — **measure distance** and **measure area** — along with a result box. After clicking a button, click points on the map; the result updates with every point.
