Finish with a double-click, Enter, or the **Selesai** ("Done") button (required on touch screens, which have no double-click). **Hapus titik** ("Remove point", or Backspace) removes the last point; **Tutup** ("Close", or Esc) clears the measurement.

While measuring, map clicks do not open popups and are not passed on to `onMapClick`, and double-clicks do not zoom.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `corner` | `"top-left"` | Map corner |
| `onResult` | — | Function `(result)` called every time a measurement finishes; `result` is the same as in `measure` |

Returns a `remove()` function.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });
addMeasureControl("peta", {
    onResult: (result) => console.log(result.text), // "886 m" or "19,64 ha · keliling 1,77 km"
});
```

## `measure(id, type, responseFunction, options)`

A measuring tool without buttons, for your own custom interface. `type` is `"distance"` (distance along the points) or `"area"` (area of the polygon formed by those points). It is used on the map the same way as `addMeasureControl`.

`responseFunction` (optional) is called once when the measurement finishes, with:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `type` | `"distance"` or `"area"` |
| `feature` | The measured GeoJSON `LineString` or `Polygon` Feature — can be saved directly or drawn with `addGeoJSON` |
| `length` | Length (distance), or perimeter (area), in meters |
| `area` | Area in square meters (`0` for distance) |
| `text` | Display-ready text, for example `"1,25 km"` or `"850 m² · keliling 120 m"` ("keliling" = perimeter) |

…or `null` if the measurement was cancelled (Esc, `stop()`, or another measurement was started).

`options.onChange` (optional) is called with the same content every time a point is added or removed.

Returns `{ finish(), undo(), stop() }`. The measured shape stays drawn after finishing, until `stop()` is called or a new measurement starts.

```javascript
const pengukur = measure("peta", "distance", (result) => {
    if (!result) return; // cancelled
    setValue("panjang-fiber", Math.round(result.length));
});
// ...
pengukur.stop();
```

`formatLength(meters)` and `formatArea(squareMeters)` — which are used for `text` — are exported too: `formatLength(12345)` → `"12,35 km"`, `formatArea(24500)` → `"2,45 ha"`.

## `addImageOverlay(id, url, options)`

Places an image (PNG, JPG, SVG) on the map: above the basemap, below the data. The image pans and zooms along with the map. Its position is set by one of:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `bounds` + `rotation` | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]`, plus `rotation` in degrees (clockwise, rotating around the image center). Suitable when the image is already roughly north-up |
| `corners` | The image's `[topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft]`, each `[lng, lat]`. These three points determine rotation, scale, and skew all at once |

Other options: `opacity` (0–1, default 1), `alt`, and `crossOrigin: true` (see PNG export below).

Returns `{ setCorners(corners), setBounds(bounds, rotation), setOpacity(opacity), remove() }` — for example for a transparency slider.

```javascript
const masterPlan = addImageOverlay("peta", "img/master-plan.png", {
    bounds: [107.5735, -6.8760, 107.5785, -6.8712],
    rotation: 12,
    opacity: 0.7,
});
masterPlan.setOpacity(0.4);
```

**From control points.** If what you know is a few points on the image (pixels) along with their lng/lat, build the transformation with [`createAffineTransform`](geomeasure#createaffinetransformfrom-to) and then compute the three corners:

```javascript
import { createAffineTransform } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geomeasure.js";

// A 2400 x 1600 pixel image; three points recognized on both the image and the map.
const piksel = [[310, 220], [2105, 260], [400, 1390]];
const lokasi = [[107.57402, -6.87188], [107.57791, -6.87201], [107.57417, -6.87458]];
const pikselKeLokasi = createAffineTransform(piksel, lokasi);

addImageOverlay("peta", "img/denah.png", {
    corners: [pikselKeLokasi([0, 0]), pikselKeLokasi([2400, 0]), pikselKeLokasi([0, 1600])],
});
```

**PDF.** Browsers cannot place a PDF directly as an image. Convert the page to PNG first — with any PDF application, or in the browser with pdf.js — then place the PNG.

## `exportMapImage(id, responseFunction, options)` and `downloadMapImage(id, filename, responseFunction, options)`

`exportMapImage` turns the current map view into a PNG image. `responseFunction(blob, info)` is called once: `blob` contains the PNG (or `null` on failure), and `info` = `{ width, height, missingImages }` — `missingImages` is the number of images that had to be skipped.

`downloadMapImage` does the same and then immediately downloads it as a file (default `"peta.png"`).

```javascript
downloadMapImage("peta", "lokasi-proyek.png");

exportMapImage("peta", (blob, info) => {
    if (!blob) return;
    if (info.missingImages > 0) console.log(info.missingImages, "images not included (server without CORS)");
    // for example, send it to the server as a report attachment
});
```

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scale` | `devicePixelRatio` | Resolution multiplier. `2` = an image twice as sharp (and larger) |
| `attribution` | `true` | `false` = no attribution text. The OpenStreetMap license requires attribution on published images |

**Included**: the basemap, overlay images, all GeoJSON layers (SVG and canvas), feature labels, markers (default pin, image icon, or custom element) with their labels, [`mapcluster.js`](mapcluster) bubbles, [`mapheat.js`](mapheat) heatmaps and grid maps, the location marker, measuring tool results, the scale bar, and attribution.
**Not included**: popups, and control buttons and panels.

Labels and HTML elements are drawn from the **browser's computed CSS**, so labels with a box background look the same as on screen: `background-color`, `border`, `border-radius`, `padding`, alignment, multi-line text (`white-space: pre`), `opacity`, and `::before`/`::after` content (for example a 📷 icon). `text-shadow` becomes a halo around the text; if its color is too similar to the text color (for example white text with a white shadow), the halo is replaced with a contrasting color so it stays legible. Not yet drawn: `box-shadow`, gradient or image backgrounds, and elements rotated with `transform`.

Browsers only allow images from other domains into a PNG if the server permits **CORS**. OpenStreetMap and Esri tiles permit it. Tiles from servers that don't are skipped (counted in `missingImages`) — the rest is still produced. For overlay images from another domain, pass `crossOrigin: true` to `addImageOverlay`, and the server must send CORS headers.

## Notes

- The measuring tools and `exportMapImage` use the `crootjsMap` interface from a `map.js` of the same version. Import all map modules from the same version tag.
- Distance and area are computed on a spherical Earth as in [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure) — the results match Turf.js, and are accurate enough for planning (cable length, zone area), not for official land boundary surveys.
- Only one measurement runs at a time per map; starting a new one cancels the old one.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapcluster

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapcluster)*

# `mapcluster.js` Module Documentation

`mapcluster.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that keeps **very large point datasets** lightweight on the map. Points that are close together on screen are merged into a single numbered bubble; as the map zooms in, the bubbles split into smaller groups, and eventually into individual points.

Without clustering, 20,000 points means 20,000 elements on the page and a map that is sluggish to pan. With this module the number of elements is determined by the screen size, not the amount of data: in testing with 100,000 points, there were never more than about 180 elements on screen.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addCluster } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcluster.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addCluster(id, geojson, options)`

Draws the point features (`Point` and `MultiPoint`) in `geojson` as clusters. `geojson` may be anything accepted by [`parseGeoJSON`](geo). Non-point features are skipped — draw lines and polygons with `addGeoJSON` from `map.js`.

Returns a `remove()` function that removes everything from the map.

```javascript
import { createMap, fitMap, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addCluster } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcluster.js";

createMap("peta");

getGeoJSON("https://api.example.com/sekolah.geojson", (response) => {
    if (!response.data) return;
    addCluster("peta", response.data);
    fitMap("peta", response.data);
});
```

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `60` | Clustering distance in pixels: points within one cell of this width are merged. The larger it is, the fewer bubbles on screen |
| `color` | blue | Color of bubbles and points (any CSS value) |
| `popup` | list of `properties` | Function `(feature) => text or DOM element` for the popup content of an individual point; returning `null` = no popup for that point. `false` = no popups at all |
| `onClick` | — | Function `(feature)` called when an individual point is clicked |

```javascript
addCluster("peta", data, {
    radius: 80,
    color: "#dc2626",
    popup: (feature) => feature.properties.nama,
});
```

## What Happens on Click

- **Bubble** — the map zooms to the center of that cluster, just enough for the cluster to split into several parts.
- **Bubble that cannot be split** — if all its members are at exactly the same position (or only separate beyond the map's maximum zoom), no zoom can separate them. Instead, a popup appears showing the count and details of the first five points.
- **Individual point** — a popup appears with its `properties` (or the content from the `popup` option), and `onClick` is called.

Clicking a bubble or point does not call the map's `onMapClick`. Dragging while pressing on a bubble still pans the map.

Large numbers in bubbles are abbreviated: `1,2rb` for 1,234, `15rb` for 15,400, `2,3jt` for 2,300,000 (Indonesian abbreviations for thousand and million). The bubble size also grows at 100 and 1,000 points.

## How It Works

At each zoom level, the world is divided into cells `radius` pixels wide. All points in one cell become one cluster, and its bubble is drawn at the centroid (average position) of its members — not at the center of the cell — so its placement follows the data.

That means a single pass over all points per zoom level, without comparing points pairwise. A level's clusters are only computed when that level is first needed, and are then cached.

In testing on a laptop with 100,000 points: initial setup took about 30 milliseconds, the first visit to a new zoom level under 10 milliseconds, and panning stayed at 60 frames per second. Phones are slower, but the pattern is the same.

## Notes

- Because the division is grid-based, two points that are close together but fall into adjacent cells are not merged, so two bubbles sometimes appear fairly close. That is the price of its speed; increase `radius` if you want fewer bubbles.
- The cluster layout changes per zoom level, so a bubble's number is not always equal to the sum of the bubbles it splits into at the next level (points at a cell edge can switch clusters). The overall total always stays the same.
- `clearMap` does not remove clusters; use the `remove()` returned by `addCluster`. To replace the data, call `remove()` and then `addCluster` again.
- The data still has to be fully downloaded and parsed by the browser. For hundreds of thousands of points, the size of the GeoJSON file itself (tens of megabytes) is usually the bottleneck, not the clustering. If your data is that large, have the backend send only the points in the visible area (see `onMapMove` and `getMapBounds` in [`map.js`](map)).
- The bubble appearance can be changed from your page's CSS via the `crootjs-cluster` (bubble) and `crootjs-cluster-point` (individual point) classes.

A complete example with 1,000 to 100,000 points: [demo](https://croot.js.org/examples/geo/cluster/) · [source](https://github.com/crootjs/examples/tree/main/geo/cluster).


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapsearch

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapsearch)*

# `mapsearch.js` Module Documentation

`mapsearch.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) for **finding places by name or address** (geocoding), **finding the address of a point** (reverse geocoding), and a ready-to-use **search box** on the map. Its size is about 3 KB gzip.

By default it uses OpenStreetMap's [Nominatim](https://nominatim.org). The public server is free but run by volunteers, with a [usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/):

- at most **1 request per second** — this module adds the delay automatically;
- **no automatic searching on every keystroke** — the search box only searches when Enter or the search button is pressed;
- results must carry **OpenStreetMap attribution** — the search box shows it below the results.

For apps with many users, run your own Nominatim (the `url` option) or use another provider (the `provider` option).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { searchPlace, reverseGeocode, addSearchControl } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapsearch.js";
```

## `addSearchControl(id, options)`

A search box in a corner of the map. Type and press Enter (or the search button); pick a result by clicking, or with the up/down arrows and Enter. The map moves to that place — the whole area if the result is a region — and places a red marker.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `placeholder` | `"Cari tempat atau alamat"` ("Search for a place or address") | Hint text in the box |
| `corner` | `"top-right"` | Map corner |
| `marker` | `true` | `false` = no red marker |
| `maxZoom` | `17` | Closest zoom when moving to a result |
| `onSelect` | — | `function (result)` when a result is selected |
| `limit`, `countryCodes`, `language`, `viewbox`, `url`, `provider` | | Same as [`searchPlace`](#searchplacequery-responsefunction-options) |

Returns `{ search(text), clear(), remove() }` — `search` runs a search from code.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 12 });
addSearchControl("peta", {
    countryCodes: "id",
    onSelect: (result) => setInnerText("lokasi", result.name),
});
```

## `searchPlace(query, responseFunction, options)`

Finds places from text: a place name, address, or street name. `responseFunction(results)` is called once, and the function also returns a Promise of `results`:

- an array of results (empty if nothing matches), or
- `null` if the request failed (network, server refused).

A single result:

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `name` | Full name of the place |
| `position` | `[lng, lat]` |
| `bbox` | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` the place's area, or `null` |
| `type` | Its type, e.g. `"amenity:university"` |
| `address` | Address details from Nominatim (`road`, `city`, `postcode`, ...), or `null` |
| `raw` | Original data from the provider |

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `5` | Number of results |
| `countryCodes` | — | Restrict countries, e.g. `"id"` or `"id,my"` |
| `language` | browser language | Language of place names, e.g. `"id"` |
| `viewbox` | — | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` to prefer results in that area |
| `url` | OSM public server | Address of your own Nominatim server |
| `provider` | — | `function (query, options) => Promise<results>` for another provider; results must be shaped like the table above |

```javascript
const hasil = await searchPlace("Jalan Asia Afrika Bandung", null, { countryCodes: "id" });
if (hasil && hasil.length) setMapView("peta", hasil[0].position, 17);
```

## `reverseGeocode(position, responseFunction, options)`

The address at point `[lng, lat]`. `responseFunction(result)` receives a single result shaped the same as above, or `null` if there is no address there or the request failed. Also returns a Promise.

`options`: `zoom` (address detail 3–18, default 18 = building level), `language`, `url`, `provider` (`function (position, options) => Promise<result>`).

```javascript
onMapClick("peta", async (position) => {
    const alamat = await reverseGeocode(position);
    showPopup("peta", position, alamat ? alamat.name : "Alamat tidak ditemukan");
});
```

## Styling

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-map-search` | The search box |
| `.crootjs-map-search-button` | The search button |
| `.crootjs-map-search-results` | Result list (`role="listbox"`); the highlighted result has `[aria-selected="true"]` |
| `.crootjs-map-search-type` | Place type below the name |
| `.crootjs-map-search-credit` | OpenStreetMap attribution |
| `.crootjs-map-search-pin` | Red marker at the selected place |


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapoffline

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapoffline)*

# `mapoffline.js` Module Documentation

`mapoffline.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that displays a base map from **a single [PMTiles](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/) file** — a single-file format for map tiles. That file can be:

- placed on an ordinary server (GitHub Pages, S3, Cloudflare R2, nginx) without a tile server: the browser reads only the pieces it needs via HTTP Range; or
- picked from the device with `<input type="file">` — the map then runs **with no internet at all**, ideal for surveys in areas without signal.

Only PMTiles version 3 containing **raster** tiles (PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF). Vector tiles (MVT) are not yet supported. Its size is about 2 KB gzip.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { openPMTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapoffline.js";
```

## `openPMTiles(source, responseFunction)`

Opens a PMTiles file. `source`: a URL, or a `File`/`Blob`.

`responseFunction(archive, error)` is called once; the function also returns a Promise of `archive`. On failure (not PMTiles, a different version, vector tiles, unsupported compression, server refused), `archive` = `null` and `error` holds the reason.

`archive` can be used directly as the `tiles` option in [`createMap`](map#createmapid-options) or [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options):

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `getTile(z, x, y)` | Promise of the tile image `Blob`, or `null` if the file has no tile there |
| `minZoom`, `maxZoom` | Zoom range present in the file |
| `bounds` | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` the file's coverage |
| `center`, `centerZoom` | Center point and zoom suggested by the file |
| `tileType` | `"image/png"`, `"image/jpeg"`, `"image/webp"`, or `"image/avif"` |
| `metadata`, `attribution` | JSON metadata inside the file, and its attribution if any |

```javascript
const arsip = await openPMTiles("https://contoh.id/peta/bandung.pmtiles");
createMap("peta", {
    tiles: arsip,
    maxNativeZoom: arsip.maxZoom, // above this, the last tiles are scaled up
    maxZoom: arsip.maxZoom + 2,
    center: arsip.center,
    zoom: arsip.centerZoom,
    attribution: arsip.attribution || "© OpenStreetMap contributors",
});
```

### Without internet

```html
<input type="file" id="berkas" accept=".pmtiles">
<div id="peta" class="peta"></div>
```

```javascript
import { onChange } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";
import { setTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";

createMap("peta", { tiles: false, center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 12 });
onChange("berkas", async () => {
    const arsip = await openPMTiles(document.getElementById("berkas").files[0]);
    if (arsip) setTiles("peta", arsip, { maxNativeZoom: arsip.maxZoom });
});
```

A file from `<input type="file">` is read directly from the device, so once the page is open the map keeps working even if the signal drops. To make the page itself open without internet too, install a *service worker* or save the page as a PWA.

## Creating PMTiles files

- [`pmtiles convert`](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/cli) converts a raster MBTiles file into PMTiles.
- Tiles downloaded with tools such as QGIS ("Generate XYZ tiles" to MBTiles) can be converted the same way.
- Make sure the source tiles' license allows storing them for offline use.

## Notes

- Supported directory compression: none and gzip (the `pmtiles` default). Brotli and zstd are not yet supported.
- The server must allow the `Range` header and, for other domains, CORS. Servers that ignore `Range` still work — the whole file is downloaded once and then read from memory.
- Tiles are displayed via *object URLs* that are released again when a tile leaves the screen, so memory does not keep growing.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapmodel

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapmodel)*

# `mapmodel.js` Module Documentation

`mapmodel.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that places **glTF/GLB 3D models at their location on the map** — e.g. a BTS tower at its real coordinates — sized to real-world meters, viewed at an angle from the south.

The CrootJS map is viewed straight down from above, so each model is drawn on its own WebGL canvas (via [`model3d.js`](model3d)) and then pinned to its point. When the map is zoomed, its size changes accordingly. This module is about 2 KB gzip, plus the `model3d.js` it imports.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addModel, setPartColor, highlightPart } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapmodel.js";
```

`mapmodel.js` **re-exports every function of [`model3d.js`](model3d)**. For models on the map, import those functions (`setPartColor`, `highlightPart`, `setPartTransform`, ...) from `mapmodel.js`, not from a separate `model3d.js` import: a module imported from another URL (for example `model3d.min.js`) is another copy with its own list of viewers, so it does not know the `viewerId` of a model on the map.

## `addModel(id, position, source, options)`

Places a model at `position` `[lng, lat]`. `source`: a `.glb`/`.gltf` URL, File/Blob, or ArrayBuffer — same as [`loadModel`](model3d#loadmodelid-source-responsefunction).

**The model's origin (0, 0, 0)** — in glTF usually the center of the model's base — lands exactly on `position`. The model's axes follow glTF: +Y up, **−Z facing north**, +X east.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `heading` | `0` | Model rotation clockwise from north, in degrees. For a BTS: the facing direction of the first sector |
| `pitch` | `50` | Viewing angle above the horizon, in degrees (`90` = straight down from above) |
| `scale` | `1` | Meters per model unit. glTF uses meters; set more than 1 to enlarge a small model so it is visible |
| `minZoom` | `13` | Below this zoom the model is hidden (too small to see) |
| `onClick` | — | `function (hit)` when the model is clicked; `hit` is the same as in [`onModelClick`](model3d#onmodelclickid-runfunction) |
| `responseFunction` | — | `function (info, error)` after the model is loaded, same as `loadModel` |

Returns:

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `setPosition([lng, lat])`, `setHeading(derajat)` | Moves or rotates the model |
| `viewerId` | Its viewer ID, for other `model3d.js` functions — e.g. `setPartColor(model.viewerId, "Antena_1", "red")` |
| `loaded` | Promise of the `loadModel` result |
| `remove()` | Removes the model and its WebGL context |

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 18 });

const bts = addModel("peta", [107.6, -6.9], "models/bts.glb", {
    heading: 30,
    onClick: (hit) => setInnerText("info", hit.path.join(" › ")),
});
await bts.loaded;
setPartColor(bts.viewerId, "Antena_1", "#f59e0b"); // highlight sector 1
```

## Notes

- **It is true to scale.** A 30 m tower at zoom 18 is only about 50 pixels. Use `scale` to exaggerate the size if the goal is a visual marker rather than the real size.
- **Each model uses one WebGL context**, and browsers limit how many there can be (usually 8–16 per page). For many locations, show a model only for the selected one, and use ordinary markers for the rest.
- The model canvas does not capture clicks and drags, so the map can still be panned from on top of the model. Clicks are checked separately against the model's shape.
- Models are always above the map's data layers and are not included in [`exportMapImage`](maptools).
- `mapmodel.js` imports `model3d.js` itself. If the page also needs a regular 3D viewer, create it with `createViewer` imported from `mapmodel.js` so that `model3d.js` is not downloaded twice.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapdraw

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapdraw)*

# `mapdraw.js` Module Documentation

`mapdraw.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) for **creating data** on the map, not just displaying it: draw points, lines, and polygons by clicking or tapping, then reshape them — drag vertices, add a vertex in the middle of a segment, delete vertices. The result is plain GeoJSON, ready to send to a server with [`postJSON`](api/) or to measure with [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure).

Useful for field surveys, marking coverage areas, drawing routes, or lot boundaries. Works with mouse and touch screens.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addDrawControl, startDrawing, editFeature } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapdraw.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addDrawControl(id, options)`

The quickest way: ready-made buttons in a corner of the map, along with a layer that displays the results.

| Button | Function |
|---|---|
| Point | Click the map to place a point. The tool stays active for the next point |
| Line | Click the points of the line; double-click or **Selesai** ("Done") to finish |
| Area | Click the boundary points; click the first point, double-click, or **Selesai** to close |
| Edit | Click a feature, then drag its handles (see [`editFeature`](#editfeatureid-feature-options)) |
| Delete | Click a feature to delete it |

The panel below the buttons shows instructions and the **Selesai** ("Done"), **Hapus titik** ("Remove point"), and **Batal** ("Cancel") buttons — required for touch screens, which have no double-click. Esc cancels.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | — | Initial GeoJSON that can be edited and deleted |
| `tools` | all | List of buttons: `["point", "line", "polygon", "edit", "delete"]` |
| `properties` | `{}` | Properties for new features: an object, or `function (type) => object` |
| `corner` | `"top-left"` | Map corner |
| `onChange` | — | `function (featureCollection)` whenever the data changes: added, edited, or deleted |

Returns `{ getData(), setData(geojson), clear(), remove() }`. `getData()` returns a copy of the FeatureCollection.

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addDrawControl } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapdraw.js";
import { postJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/api.js";
import { onClick } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 16 });
const gambar = addDrawControl("peta", {
    properties: (type) => ({ jenis: type, dibuat: new Date().toISOString() }),
});

onClick("simpan", async () => {
    const { status } = await postJSON("https://api.example.com/survei", gambar.getData(), null);
    console.log(status === 200 ? "Tersimpan" : "Gagal: " + status);
});
```

## `startDrawing(id, type, responseFunction, options)`

Draws **one** geometry, for your own custom interface. `type`: `"point"`, `"line"`, or `"polygon"` (or their GeoJSON names: `"Point"`, `"LineString"`, `"Polygon"`).

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Click / tap the map | Adds a point. A point (`"point"`) finishes immediately |
| Click the polygon's first point | Closes the polygon |
| Double-click, or Enter | Finish |
| Backspace | Removes the last point |
| Esc | Cancel |

While drawing, map clicks do not open popups and are not passed on to `onMapClick`; panning the map still works.

`responseFunction(feature)` is called once: with the resulting GeoJSON Feature, or `null` if cancelled. Coordinates are rounded to 7 decimal places (about 1 cm), and polygons are always closed (last point = first point).

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `properties` | Properties of the resulting Feature: an object, or `function (type) => object` |
| `onChange` | `function (feature)` whenever a point is added or removed — `null` while there are not yet enough points |

Returns `{ finish(), undo(), stop() }` for your own Done, Remove point, and Cancel buttons.

```javascript
import { getArea } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geomeasure.js";

onClick("gambar-kavling", () => {
    startDrawing("peta", "polygon", (feature) => {
        if (!feature) return; // cancelled
        setInnerText("luas", Math.round(getArea(feature)) + " m²");
    });
});
```

## `editFeature(id, feature, options)`

Shows handles for reshaping a geometry:

| Handle | Action |
|---|---|
| White circle at each vertex | Drag to move the vertex |
| Small orange circle at the middle of a segment | Drag to add a vertex there |
| Double-click a vertex (mouse), or long-press for 0.5 seconds (touch screen) | Deletes the vertex — lines need at least 2 vertices, areas 3 |

`feature` may be a Feature or just a geometry: `Point`, `LineString`, `Polygon`, or their `Multi` versions, including polygons with holes. The original data is not modified. Dragging a handle does not pan the map.

`options.onChange(feature)` is called after each drag, vertex addition, or vertex deletion, in the same shape as the input (a Feature stays a Feature, properties included).

Returns `{ getFeature(), stop() }`. Only one `editFeature` is active per map; calling it again stops the previous one.

```javascript
const editor = editFeature("peta", batasKavling, {
    onChange: (feature) => postJSON("https://api.example.com/kavling/7", feature, null),
});
onClick("selesai", () => editor.stop());
```

## Styling

Everything can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`.

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `svg.crootjs-draw` | Drawing layers (one for the drawing in progress, one for the `addDrawControl` results, one for the edit handles) |
| `.crootjs-draw-shape`, `.crootjs-draw-line` | Area/line; line without fill |
| `.crootjs-draw-preview` | Dashed guide line to the cursor position |
| `.crootjs-draw-editing` | The shape being edited |
| `circle.crootjs-draw-point` | Points from `addDrawControl` |
| `circle.crootjs-draw-vertex`, `-vertex-first` | Vertex; the polygon's first vertex (click to close) |
| `circle.crootjs-draw-midpoint` | Segment midpoint |
| `.crootjs-map-draw`, `.crootjs-map-draw-tool`, `.crootjs-map-draw-panel`, `.crootjs-map-draw-actions` | Control box, tool buttons (the active one has `aria-pressed="true"`), instruction panel, and its action buttons |

On touch screens the handles are automatically larger.

## Notes

- Drawings pan and zoom along with the map. The layers are SVG above the `addGeoJSON` data, so they are not yet included by `exportMapImage`.
- To display finalized data with styles, popups, and labels, pass the result to [`addGeoJSON`](map#addgeojsonid-geojson-options). `mapdraw.js` is for creating and editing data.
- The [`maptools.js`](maptools) measuring tools and `startDrawing` both "borrow" map clicks; only one is active at a time.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapheat

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapheat)*

# `mapheat.js` Module Documentation

`mapheat.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that draws point data as a **heatmap** (a smooth density gradient) or a **grid map** (square/hexagon cells colored by their average value, like the nPerf signal coverage map). Both are drawn on a single canvas above the basemap and below the data layers, so they stay lightweight even for tens of thousands of points: in testing, 50,000 points were redrawn in about 15–25 ms.

It is separate from `map.js` so that pages that don't use it don't have to download it (about 6 KB gzip, plus [`geo.js`](geo) for reading GeoJSON).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { addHeatmap, addGridMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapheat.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

**Data** for both functions can be:

- any GeoJSON accepted by [`parseGeoJSON`](geo) — only `Point` and `MultiPoint` features are used, other features are skipped; or
- an array of `[lng, lat]`, or `[lng, lat, value]` — more economical for large data from your own server.

## `addHeatmap(id, data, options)`

Draws point density as a color gradient: blue where it is sparse, red where it is densest. Each point "heats up" its surroundings, fully at the point itself and fading out completely at a distance of `radius`.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `weight` | `1` | Weight of each point: a property name, or `function(feature) => number`. For array data: the third element if present. Points with a weight of 0, a negative weight, or a non-numeric weight are skipped |
| `radius` | `30` | Influence distance of each point, in screen pixels. Stays the same at every zoom |
| `radiusMeters` | — | Influence distance in meters (replaces `radius`): grows as you zoom in, suitable when "heat" means a distance on the ground |
| `max` | automatic | The density treated as hottest. Default: the highest density currently on screen, like the Google Maps heatmap. Set a fixed number so colors can be compared across places and over time |
| `scale` | `"linear"` | `"linear"`, `"sqrt"`, or `"log"`: how density is mapped to color. `"sqrt"`/`"log"` bring out sparse areas when the data is piled up at just a few points |
| `gradient` | blue → red | `{ position 0..1: color }`, for example `{ 0.4: "blue", 0.7: "lime", 1: "red" }` |
| `opacity` | `0.8` | Opacity of the whole layer (0–1) |
| `legend` | `false` | `true`, or `{ title, corner, low, high }`: a gradient legend in a corner of the map (defaults: `"bottom-right"`, text `"Kepadatan"`, `"Rendah"`, `"Tinggi"` — Indonesian for "Density", "Low", "High") |

Returns `{ setData(data), setOptions(options), show(), hide(), remove() }`.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 13 });

// Outage reports from customers; weight = number of complaints at that location.
const heat = addHeatmap("peta", laporan, {
    weight: "keluhan",
    radius: 35,
    legend: { title: "Keluhan pelanggan" },
});

heat.setOptions({ scale: "sqrt" }); // bring out areas with few complaints
heat.setData(laporanBaru);          // replace the data without recreating the layer
```

## `addGridMap(id, data, options)`

Groups points into square or hexagon cells, then colors each cell by the combined value of the points inside it — for example the average RSRP from a drive test, like the nPerf coverage map. Click a cell to see its value.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | — | Value of each point: a property name, or `function(feature) => number`. For array data: the third element. Points without a numeric value are skipped. Without `value`, cells are computed from the number of points |
| `aggregate` | `"mean"` | How values in one cell are combined: `"mean"`, `"max"`, `"min"`, `"sum"`, or `"count"`. Without `value`, always `"count"` |
| `shape` | `"square"` | `"square"` or `"hex"` (hexagon) |
| `cellSize` | `32` | Cell width in screen pixels. Cells are regrouped at each zoom level, so their on-screen size stays fixed: zoomed out, one cell covers a wider area |
| `cellMeters` | — | Cell width in meters (replaces `cellSize`, minimum 2): cells stay fixed on the ground and grow as you zoom in, like a coverage map. The meter calculation uses the data's average latitude |
| `breaks` | automatic | `[{ value, color, label }]`: cells with a value `>= value` use that `color`; cells below the first break use the first color. `label` is optional, for the legend |
| `colors` | red → green | Colors for automatic breaks, from low to high values. Default is 5 red–yellow–green colors, suited to values where higher is better (signal, speed) |
| `opacity` | `0.7` | Layer opacity (0–1) |
| `stroke` | — | Cell outline color. Default is no outline |
| `popup` | value + number of points | `function(cell) => text or element` when a cell is clicked; `false` = no popup |
| `onClick` | — | `function(cell)` called when a cell is clicked |
| `legend` | `false` | `true`, or `{ title, corner }`: a color legend in a corner of the map (default `"bottom-right"`) |

Without `breaks`, the range of cell values is divided evenly across `colors`. Automatic breaks are computed from the cells at the zoom level currently shown, so with `cellSize` the legend can change as you zoom. Set your own `breaks` so the colors stay fixed and comparable, for example standard RSRP thresholds.

The `cell` received by `popup` and `onClick`:

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `value` | The cell's value according to `aggregate` |
| `count` | Number of points in the cell |
| `mean`, `min`, `max`, `sum` | Summary of its points' values |
| `center` | `[lng, lat]` center point of the cell |
| `color`, `label` | The cell's color and its legend label |

Returns `{ setData(data), setOptions(options), show(), hide(), remove(), cellAt(position) }`. `cellAt([lng, lat])` gives the `cell` at that point at the zoom level currently shown, or `null` if there is no cell there or the layer is hidden. Use it for an [`addContextMenu`](mapcontrol#addcontextmenuid-items-options) right-click menu, or to show a cell's value in your own panel.

```javascript
// Drive test results: each point has an rsrp property (dBm).
addGridMap("peta", driveTest, {
    value: "rsrp",
    shape: "hex",
    cellMeters: 100,
    breaks: [
        { value: -140, color: "#d7191c", label: "Sangat lemah (< -110)" },
        { value: -110, color: "#fdae61", label: "Lemah" },
        { value: -100, color: "#ffffbf", label: "Sedang" },
        { value: -90, color: "#a6d96a", label: "Baik" },
        { value: -80, color: "#1a9641", label: "Sangat baik (≥ -80)" },
    ],
    legend: { title: "RSRP (dBm)" },
    popup: (cell) => `RSRP rata-rata ${cell.value.toFixed(1)} dBm dari ${cell.count} pengukuran`,
});
```

Array data can be used directly too — its third element becomes the value:

```javascript
addGridMap("peta", [[107.601, -6.902, -87], [107.603, -6.901, -95] /* ... */], { legend: true });
```

## Styling

The legend uses the following classes, which can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`:

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-heat-legend` | Legend box |
| `.crootjs-heat-legend-title` | Legend title |
| `.crootjs-heat-legend-row`, `.crootjs-heat-legend-swatch` | Color row and its color swatch (`addGridMap`) |
| `.crootjs-heat-legend-bar`, `.crootjs-heat-legend-ends` | Gradient bar and the "Rendah"/"Tinggi" ("Low"/"High") text (`addHeatmap`) |
| `canvas.crootjs-heat-canvas` | The layer's canvas |

## Notes

- While the map is being panned or zoomed, the existing image just moves and scales along with it; as soon as the map pauses briefly (about 0.1 seconds), the layer is redrawn precisely. During zoom, the gradient may look blurry for a moment — that is normal.
- Heatmaps and grid maps are always below `addGeoJSON` layers and markers. Clicking an `addGeoJSON` feature opens that feature's popup, not the popup of the cell underneath.
- Included in exports by [`exportMapImage`](maptools#exportmapimageid-responsefunction-options-and-downloadmapimageid-filename-responsefunction-options) in `maptools.js`. The legend is not, because map controls are not exported.
- Very large data (hundreds of thousands of points) still works, but send it as a `[lng, lat, value]` array instead of GeoJSON to save memory and parse faster.
- A heatmap shows **density** (where there are many points). To show a **value** at a place (for example signal strength), use `addGridMap` with `value` — a heatmap weighted by signal value would be misleading, because places with many measurements look "hot" even when the signal is weak.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/model3d

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../model3d)*

# `model3d.js` Module Documentation

`model3d.js` displays **glTF 2.0** 3D models (`.glb` and `.gltf`) directly in the browser: rotate, zoom, click a part, change its color, hide it, or change its position and rotation from code. Everything is written from scratch on top of WebGL — its own GLB binary parser, matrices, shaders, and orbit controls — without Three.js (about 600 KB) or any other library. Its size is about 16 KB gzip.

It renders with **WebGL2**, and automatically falls back to **WebGL1** in older browsers. On-screen move/rotate gizmos, HTML labels pinned to the model, animation, exploded view, cross-sections, and `.glb` export live in the add-on module [`model3dtools.js`](model3dtools).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createViewer, loadModel } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/model3d.js";
```

## Minimal Example

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
<div id="model" class="model"></div>
<output id="status"></output>
<script type="module" src="index.js"></script>
```

```css
/* style.css — the viewer fills its element, so a height is required */
.model { height: 420px; }
```

```javascript
// index.js
import { createViewer, loadModel, onModelClick, highlightPart } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/model3d.js";
import { setInnerText } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";

createViewer("model");
loadModel("model", "models/bts.glb", (info, error) => {
    if (!info) return setInnerText("status", "Gagal: " + error);
    setInnerText("status", `${info.parts.length} bagian, ${info.triangles} segitiga`);
});

onModelClick("model", (hit) => {
    highlightPart("model", hit ? hit.part : null);
    setInnerText("status", hit ? hit.path.join(" › ") : "—");
});
```

## `createViewer(id, options)`

Creates a viewer inside element `id` (usually a `<div>`). The element must have a height set from CSS. Calling it again with the same `id` recreates the viewer.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | light gray gradient | Background, any CSS `background` value (`"#1a1a1a"`, a gradient, `"transparent"`) |
| `autoRotate` | `0` | Degrees per second the model spins on its own. Stops as soon as the user touches it |
| `fov` | `45` | Camera's vertical field of view, in degrees |
| `controls` | `true` | `false` = no user rotate/zoom/pan, e.g. for a static product view |
| `webgl` | `2` | `1` = force WebGL1, to test how it looks in older browsers |
| `dracoDecoder` | from `www.gstatic.com` | Folder of the Draco decoder (`draco_wasm_wrapper_gltf.js` + `draco_decoder_gltf.wasm`) for Draco-compressed models. Set it to your own folder if the app must not depend on Google's servers |

If the browser has no WebGL at all, the viewer shows a message and every other function does nothing.

## `loadModel(id, source, responseFunction)`

Loads a model, replacing the previous one. The camera is adjusted automatically so the whole model is visible.

- `source` — URL of a `.glb`/`.gltf` file, a **File/Blob** (e.g. from `<input type="file">`), or an `ArrayBuffer`.
- `responseFunction(info, error)` — called once the model is displayed. `info` contains:

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `parts` | Names of all parts (nodes), in tree order |
| `triangles` | Number of triangles |
| `bounds` | `{ min, max, center, size }` the model's bounding box, in model units (glTF uses meters) |

On failure, `info` = `null` and `error` holds the reason (also printed to the console). `loadModel` also returns a Promise of the same `info`, so it can be `await`ed.

```javascript
// Opening a file from the user's computer
import { onChange } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/element.js";

onChange("file", () => {
    loadModel("model", document.getElementById("file").files[0], (info, error) => {
        console.log(info || error);
    });
});
```

For a `.gltf` that uses separate `.bin` and image files, those files are downloaded from the same folder as the `.gltf` URL. From `<input type="file">`, only `.glb` or `.gltf` with embedded data can be opened, because the companion files are not selected along with it.

## Model Parts

A glTF model is built from nested **nodes** — e.g. `Menara` › `Sektor_1` › `Antena_1`. In this module nodes are called **parts**, and they are looked up by name (the node name, or its mesh name if the node is unnamed). Changes to a part (color, hiding, position) also apply to all parts beneath it. If several nodes share the same name, all of them change.

### `getParts(id)`

List of all parts, in tree order: `[{ name, mesh, parent, depth, visible }]`. `depth` = depth in the tree (0 = top level), useful for building an indented list.

### `setPartColor(id, name, color)`

Changes a part's color. `color`: any CSS color (`"#ff0000"`, `"red"`, `"rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)"`) or `[r, g, b, a]` in 0..1. Alpha below 1 makes it transparent. `null` = back to its original color. The new color replaces that part's texture. Returns `false` if the part does not exist.

### `setPartVisible(id, name, visible)`

Shows (`true`) or hides (`false`) a part.

### `highlightPart(id, name)`

Marks the currently selected part in blue. `null` = remove the highlight. Only one name is highlighted at a time.

### `getPartTransform(id, name)` and `setPartTransform(id, name, transform)`

A part's position, rotation, and scale **relative to its parent** — the same as the `translation`, `rotation`, and `scale` values in the glTF file.

`getPartTransform` returns:

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `position` | `[x, y, z]` |
| `rotation` | `[x, y, z]` degrees, Euler in XYZ order (same as Blender and Three.js) |
| `quaternion` | `[x, y, z, w]` the same rotation |
| `scale` | `[x, y, z]` |

`setPartTransform` changes only what is given: `position`, `rotation` (`[x, y, z]` degrees, or a quaternion `[x, y, z, w]`), and `scale` (a number, or `[x, y, z]`).

```javascript
// Azimuth 150° and downtilt 6° for the sector 2 antenna. glTF's Y axis points up.
setPartTransform("model", "Sektor_2", { rotation: [0, -150, 0] });
setPartTransform("model", "Antena_2", { rotation: [6, 0, 0] });
```

## `onModelClick(id, runFunction)`

`runFunction(hit)` is called every time the model is clicked or tapped (rotating does not count as a click):

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `part` | Name of the lowest part that was hit |
| `mesh` | Its mesh name, or `null` |
| `path` | Part names from the top down to `part`, e.g. `["BTS", "Menara", "Sektor_1", "Lengan_1", "Antena_1"]` — for selecting the group rather than its small piece |
| `position` | `[x, y, z]` the hit point, in model coordinates |
| `distance` | Distance from the camera |

`hit` = `null` if the background was clicked. Returns a `stop()` function.

## Camera

### `fitView(id, name)`

Smoothly moves the camera so the whole model fits on screen. With `name`, only that part; `name` may also be an array of names, e.g. `["Sektor_1", "Sektor_2", "Sektor_3"]`.

### `setCameraView(id, view, animate = true)` and `getCameraView(id)`

`view` = `{ yaw, pitch, distance, target }`, only what is given:

- `yaw` — angle around the model, in degrees. 0 = from the front (the +Z direction).
- `pitch` — angle from above, in degrees, -89 to 89.
- `distance` — distance from the camera to `target`, in model units.
- `target` — `[x, y, z]` the point being looked at.

`getCameraView` returns the same values. Save them and set them again to "bookmark" a viewpoint.

### `setAutoRotate(id, degreesPerSecond)`

Spins the model continuously; `0` = stop. It also stops as soon as the user touches the model.

## `clearModel(id)` and `removeViewer(id)`

`clearModel` removes the model but keeps the viewer. `removeViewer` removes the viewer along with its WebGL context; the element itself remains.

## Built-in Interactions

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Drag with the mouse or one finger | rotates the model |
| Right-click + drag, Shift/Ctrl + drag, or two-finger drag | pans the view |
| Mouse wheel / pinch | zoom |
| Double-click | centers the camera on that point and moves closer |
| Click / tap | `onModelClick` |
| Arrow keys (when the viewer has focus) | rotate by 10° |
| `+` / `-` (when the viewer has focus) | zoom |

Users who enable *reduce motion* in their system get camera moves without animation and no auto-rotation.

## glTF Support

| Supported | Not yet supported |
|---|---|
| `.glb` and `.gltf` (embedded buffer, `data:` URI, or a separate `.bin` file) | meshopt compression — re-export without compression |
| **Draco** compression (`KHR_draco_mesh_compression`), see the [Draco notes](#draco) | |
| Nested nodes with `matrix` or translation/rotation/scale | |
| ***Skinning*** — characters or organs whose surface bends to follow bones, up to 64 bones per mesh | More than 64 bones (or more than the GPU can handle) — shown in a rest pose, with a warning |
| Node animation, played with [`playAnimation`](model3dtools#getanimationsid-and-playanimationid-animation-options) in `model3dtools.js` | |
| Base color, color textures (PNG/JPEG), per-vertex color (`COLOR_0`) | Normal maps, *occlusion*, and metallic/roughness textures |
| `metallicFactor`, `roughnessFactor`, `emissiveFactor` | *Morph targets*, cameras and lights from the file |
| Transparent (`BLEND`) and cutout (`MASK`), double-sided | `KHR_texture_transform` and other material extensions |
| All accessor types (Float32, Int8/16, Uint8/16/32), interleaved data, sparse | |
| `KHR_materials_unlit`, `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`, `KHR_mesh_quantization` | |

### Draco

Draco-compressed models (many models from Sketchfab and from export tools that shrink files) are decoded with **Google's official decoder** in WebAssembly. That decoder (about 300 KB) is downloaded only when a model that uses it is loaded — pages with ordinary models download nothing extra. By default it comes from `www.gstatic.com`; for apps that must run without Google's servers, copy both decoder files to your own server and set the `dracoDecoder` option.

### Skinning

Skinned meshes are driven by their bones (glTF nodes), so animation from [`playAnimation`](model3dtools#getanimationsid-and-playanimationid-animation-options) or `setPartTransform` on a bone bends the surface directly. Clicks and bounding boxes (`fitView`, hotspots) use the bone-deformed positions.

The lighting is simple: sky/ground light plus one directional light that follows the camera, with shininess based on `roughness`. It is enough to see shape and color clearly, but it is not full PBR with environment maps like Three.js or `<model-viewer>`.

## Styling

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-3d` | The viewer (contains the canvas and overlay). Its default background is set here and can be overridden from the page's CSS |
| `.crootjs-3d-loading` | Added to `.crootjs-3d` while a model is loading, e.g. to show a *spinner* |
| `.crootjs-3d-dragging` | Added while the model is being rotated/panned |
| `canvas.crootjs-3d-canvas` | The WebGL canvas |
| `.crootjs-3d-overlay` | HTML layer above the canvas (where hotspots and gizmos go) |

## Writing Your Own Add-on

`createViewer` attaches a small interface to its element, in the `crootjs3d` property. That is how [`model3dtools.js`](model3dtools) works without importing `model3d.js` (which would load a second copy with a separate list of viewers).

| `crootjs3d` member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `root`, `canvas`, `overlay` | The viewer element, its canvas, and the HTML layer above it |
| `requestRender()` | Requests a redraw on the next frame |
| `onRender(runFunction)` | Called after every draw; returns `stop()` |
| `onModel(runFunction)` | Called every time the model is replaced or removed; returns `stop()` |
| `camera()` | `{ eye, target, forward, right, up, viewProj, fov, width, height }` |
| `toScreen([x, y, z])` | Model point → `[x, y, depth]` pixels on the canvas, or `null` if behind the camera |
| `rayAt([x, y])`, `raycast(origin, direction, skip?)` | A ray from the camera through a screen point, and the first surface hit: `{ node, t, position }` |
| `findParts(name)`, `isShown(node)`, `boundsOf(nodes)` | Nodes named `name`, whether they are shown, and their bounding box |
| `getTransform(node)`, `setTransform(node, transform)` | Same as `getPartTransform`/`setPartTransform`, for a single node |
| `getModel()` | The loaded model: `{ source: { json, buffers, images }, nodes, roots }` |
| `readAccessor(index)` | glTF accessor data: `{ array, size, componentType, normalized, count }` |
| `update()` | After a node's `translation`/`rotation`/`scale` is changed directly (e.g. by animation), recompute and redraw |
| `setClip(plane, cap)` | Clipping plane `[nx, ny, nz, w]` (points with `n·p + w > 0` are discarded) and the color of the cut surface; `null` = no clipping |
| `parseColor(color)` | CSS color → linear `[r, g, b, a]` |

## Notes

- **No WebGPU.** A second backend would double the module's size, while WebGL2 is already available in nearly every browser and WebGL1 covers the rest.
- Models from other domains must allow CORS. Files opened directly from disk (`file://`) cannot be `fetch`ed; run through a local server, or open the file with `<input type="file">`.
- glTF units are meters with the Y axis up. Models from CAD applications that use millimeters will appear 1000× larger — the camera still adjusts, but `position` and `bounds` are in those units.
- Clicks are computed on the CPU against every triangle. A million-triangle model takes about 1 ms per click; no problem for ordinary models.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/model3dtools

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../model3dtools)*

# `model3dtools.js` Module Documentation

`model3dtools.js` is an add-on module for [`model3d.js`](model3d) with tools for apps that modify a model rather than just display it:

- **Hotspots** — HTML labels pinned to a point or part of the model that move with it as the model rotates, and dim when hidden behind it.
- **Gizmo** — move, rotate, and scale handles for changing a part directly on screen with a mouse or finger.
- **Animation** — plays the animations stored in the glTF file, with play/pause/scrub controls.
- **Exploded view** — spreads the model's parts away from their center, like an assembly drawing.
- **Cross-section** — slices the model with a plane to see its inside.
- **AR** — opens the model in the room through the phone camera (Scene Viewer on Android, AR Quick Look on iPhone).
- **GLB export** — saves the model with all its changes as a new `.glb` file.

The middle three suit learning materials well: anatomy, engines, buildings, lab equipment. This module is separate from `model3d.js` so pages that only display a model don't have to download it (about 8 KB gzip).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createViewer, loadModel } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/model3d.js";
import { addHotspot, enableTransform, getAnimations, playAnimation, explodeModel, addSection, addARButton, getARLink, exportGLB, downloadGLB } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/model3dtools.js";
```

The viewer must already be created with `createViewer`. Hotspots and gizmos that refer to a part name need the model to be loaded, so call them inside `loadModel`'s `responseFunction`.

## `addHotspot(id, anchor, content, options)`

Pins an HTML element or text to the model.

- `anchor` — a **part name** (pinned to the center of that part, and follows it if the part is moved), or **`[x, y, z]`** model coordinates.
- `content` — a DOM element (moved on top of the viewer), or text.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `at` | `"center"` | `"top"` = center of that part's top side, good for a label above an object |
| `offset` | `[0, 0, 0]` | Extra offset in model units, e.g. `[0, 0.5, 0]` slightly above it |
| `occlude` | `true` | The label is dimmed (class `.crootjs-3d-hotspot-hidden`) when its point is hidden behind another part of the model. `false` = always clear |
| `onClick` | — | Function called when the label is clicked |
| `className` | — | Extra CSS class |

Returns a `remove()` function. The hotspot is also hidden when its part is hidden with `setPartVisible`.

```javascript
loadModel("model", "models/bts.glb", () => {
    addHotspot("model", "Antena_1", "Sektor 1 · 0°", { at: "top" });
    addHotspot("model", "Kabinet", "Kabinet BBU", { onClick: () => tampilkanDetail("Kabinet") });
    addHotspot("model", [0, 30, 0], "Puncak 30 m");
});
```

For a label whose content changes (e.g. a sensor reading), pass your own element and change its content any time — the hotspot does not need to be recreated:

```javascript
const nilai = document.createElement("span");
addHotspot("model", "Antena_1", nilai, { at: "top" });
nilai.textContent = "RSRP -87 dBm";
```

## `enableTransform(id, name, mode, onChange)`

Shows a gizmo on part `name` so it can be changed directly on screen. There is only one gizmo per viewer: calling it again moves the gizmo to another part.

| `mode` | Handles | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `"translate"` | Red/green/blue arrows for the X/Y/Z axes | Moves along that axis |
| `"rotate"` | Three rings | Rotates around that axis. Hold **Shift** for 15° steps |
| `"scale"` | Boxes at the axis ends, plus an orange box in the center | Scales one axis, or uniformly |

`onChange(info)` is called continuously while dragging, and once more on release. `info` is the same as [`getPartTransform`](model3d#getparttransformid-name-and-setparttransformid-name-transform) plus `part` (the part name) and `dragging` (`false` on the last call — the right moment to save to a server).

The move and rotate axes follow the part's **parent** axes, so they match the reported `position` and `rotation` values. The scale axes follow the part itself. While a handle is being dragged, the camera does not rotate.

Returns `{ setMode(mode), remove() }`. The gizmo disappears on its own when the model is replaced.

```javascript
let gizmo = null;

onModelClick("model", (hit) => {
    if (gizmo) gizmo.remove();
    gizmo = hit ? enableTransform("model", hit.part, "rotate", (info) => {
        if (!info.dragging) simpanKeServer(info.part, info.rotation);
    }) : null;
});

onClick("mode-geser", () => gizmo && gizmo.setMode("translate"));
```

## `getAnimations(id)` and `playAnimation(id, animation, options)`

`getAnimations` gives the list of animations in the model file: `[{ index, name, duration }]`, `duration` in seconds. A model without animations gives `[]`.

`playAnimation` plays an animation. `animation` = its name or index (default `0`, the first one).

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loop` | `true` | `false` = stop at the end |
| `speed` | `1` | Speed: `0.5` = half, `2` = double, negative = backwards |
| `autoplay` | `true` | `false` = prepared but not yet running, e.g. to be driven by a slider |
| `onUpdate` | — | Function `(time, duration)` every frame, e.g. to move a time slider |
| `onEnd` | — | Function called when the animation finishes (only with `loop: false`) |

Returns a controller:

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `play()`, `pause()` | Play and pause |
| `stop()` | Stops and returns the parts to their positions before the animation |
| `seek(seconds)` | Jumps to a given second, including while paused — for a time slider |
| `setSpeed(speed)`, `isPlaying()`, `time()`, `duration` | Speed, whether it is playing, current time, and the animation's length |

```javascript
loadModel("model", "models/mesin.glb", () => {
    const animasi = playAnimation("model", "Langkah_Hisap", {
        loop: false,
        onUpdate: (time) => setValue("waktu", time),
    });
    onInput("waktu", () => animasi.seek(Number(getValue("waktu"))));
});
```

What gets played is **node** motion (position, rotation, scale) with `STEP`, `LINEAR`, and `CUBICSPLINE` interpolation — enough for engines, gears, doors, assemblies, or orbiting planets. Animations that bend the surface (*skinning*, e.g. a walking character, and *morph targets*) are not yet supported: the bones move, but the surface stays still.

## `explodeModel(id, amount, options)`

Spreads the model's parts away from their center. `amount`: `0` = together (original positions), `1` = fully separated, values in between are allowed — good for a slider.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `part` | automatic | Name of the part whose **children** are separated. Default: the first level from the top that branches |
| `distance` | `1` | Distance multiplier. With `1`, at `amount` 1 each part's distance from the center doubles |
| `animate` | `true` | `false` = move instantly. Use `false` for values from a slider, so it follows the finger without lag |

Each part moves straight away from its group's center. Going back to `0` restores the original positions exactly; the positions at that moment also become the reference for the next separation.

```javascript
onInput("pisah", () => {
    explodeModel("model", Number(getValue("pisah")), { part: "Mesin", animate: false });
});
```

Animation, the gizmo, and the exploded view all change part positions. Return the exploded view to `0` before playing an animation or using the gizmo on the same parts.

## `addSection(id, options)`

Slices the model with a plane. The cut-away side is not drawn and cannot be clicked; the cut surface is filled with a flat color, so hollow objects look like solids split open. Hotspots whose points are cut away are hidden.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axis` | `"x"` | `"x"` = vertical plane splitting left-right, `"z"` = vertical front-back, `"y"` = horizontal; or `[x, y, z]` the direction of a tilted plane |
| `position` | `0.5` | Position of the plane along that axis: `0` = the model's lower end (model whole), `1` = upper end (model gone) |
| `flip` | `false` | `true` = the opposite side is discarded |
| `color` | the part's color, darkened | CSS color of the cut surface, e.g. `"#facc15"` to make the slice stand out |

Only one section per viewer; calling again replaces the old one. Returns `{ set(options), remove() }` — `set` changes some of the options, e.g. from a slider:

```javascript
const potongan = addSection("model", { axis: "x", color: "#facc15" });
onInput("letak", () => potongan.set({ position: Number(getValue("letak")) }));
onClick("utuh", () => potongan.remove());
```

## `addARButton(id, url, options)` and `getARLink(url, options)`

A **"Lihat di AR"** ("View in AR") button in the corner of the viewer: the model is placed in the real room through the phone camera, and can be moved and rotated with a finger.

| Device | What happens |
|---|---|
| Android | Opens **Scene Viewer** (Google's app) with the `url` file |
| iPhone/iPad | Opens **AR Quick Look** — only if `options.usdz` is set, because Quick Look cannot open `.glb`. Convert it to `.usdz` first (e.g. with Apple's Reality Converter) |
| Others (desktop) | The button is not added |

`url` must be a `.glb`/`.gltf` file publicly downloadable over HTTPS — not a local file or a `blob:` from `exportGLB`, because another app opens it.

`options` (all optional): `title` (title in Scene Viewer), `usdz` (file for iPhone/iPad), `label` (default "Lihat di AR"), `mode` (`"ar_preferred"` default, `"ar_only"`, `"3d_only"`), `fallback` (page to use if Scene Viewer is not available; default this page).

Returns `{ supported, remove() }` — `supported` = `false` if the button was not added on this device.

`getARLink(url, options)` gives just the Scene Viewer link, for your own button or QR code.

```javascript
loadModel("model", "https://contoh.id/models/bts.glb", () => {
    addARButton("model", "https://contoh.id/models/bts.glb", { title: "Menara BTS", usdz: "https://contoh.id/models/bts.usdz" });
});
```

## `exportGLB(id, responseFunction)` and `downloadGLB(id, filename, responseFunction)`

Assembles the currently displayed model into a single `.glb` file, with all its changes:

- position, rotation, and scale from the gizmo or `setPartTransform`;
- colors from `setPartColor` (that part gets a new material, so other parts using the same material are not changed);
- parts hidden with `setPartVisible` are removed from the scene;
- external buffers and textures of a `.gltf` model are packed into the single file.

`exportGLB` passes a `Blob` (type `model/gltf-binary`) to `responseFunction(blob)` and also returns it as a Promise — e.g. for uploading to a server. `downloadGLB` downloads it directly as `filename` (default `"model.glb"`). If there is no model yet, `blob` = `null`.

```javascript
onClick("unduh", () => downloadGLB("model", "bts-editan.glb"));

// or upload to a server
onClick("simpan", async () => {
    const form = new FormData();
    form.append("model", await exportGLB("model"), "bts.glb");
    fetch("https://contoh.server/api/model", { method: "POST", body: form });
});
```

The resulting file can be opened again with `loadModel`, in Blender, or in other glTF viewers.

## Styling

Everything can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`.

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-3d-hotspot` | Hotspot label. The blue dot below it is `::after` |
| `.crootjs-3d-hotspot-hidden` | A hotspot whose point is hidden by the model (default: dimmed) |
| `.crootjs-3d-hotspot-clickable` | A hotspot that has `onClick` |
| `a.crootjs-3d-ar` | The "Lihat di AR" button |
| `svg.crootjs-3d-gizmo` | The gizmo |
| `.crootjs-3d-gizmo-x`, `-y`, `-z`, `-all` | Color of each axis (via `color`), and the uniform-scale handle |
| `.crootjs-3d-gizmo-line`, `-knob`, `-hit` | The visible line/ring, the handle tip, and the click area wider than the line |

## Notes

- The gizmo and hotspots are drawn as SVG/HTML on top of the canvas, so they stay sharp and are easy to style, and the gizmo is always visible even when its part is hidden behind another.
- For a part name used by several nodes: the gizmo grabs the first one, the hotspot is pinned to the center of all of them.
- Export copies the original model data as-is; old meshes and materials that are no longer used stay in the file (still valid, just slightly larger).


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/geomeasure

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../geomeasure)*

# `geomeasure.js` Module Documentation

`geomeasure.js` contains the calculations most often needed for geospatial data: distance, length, area, point-in-area, nearest point, radius circles, and transformation from local coordinate systems. They are all pure functions — no map, no DOM required — so they can be used with or without [`map.js`](map).

Positions are always `[lng, lat]` as in GeoJSON, and results are always in **meters** (or square meters).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { getDistance, getArea, isInside, createAffineTransform } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geomeasure.js";
```

Functions that accept `geojson` are as flexible as [`parseGeoJSON`](geo): a `FeatureCollection`, a single `Feature`, a single bare geometry, an array of them, or JSON text. The examples below use `data` from [contoh.geojson](https://github.com/petapedia/geojson/blob/main/contoh.geojson).

## `getDistance(from, to)`

The distance between two positions, following the curvature of the Earth.

```javascript
getDistance([106.8272, -6.1754], [107.6191, -6.9175]); // 120258.27... (Monas to Bandung's town square, about 120 km)
```

## `getLength(geojson)`

The length of all lines in the data. For polygons, the perimeter is counted (including hole edges). Points have no length.

```javascript
getLength({ type: "LineString", coordinates: [[107.60, -6.90], [107.61, -6.90], [107.61, -6.91]] }); // 2215.84...
getLength(data.features[0]); // 110.70... (perimeter of the Rektorat building)
```

## `getArea(geojson)`

The area of all polygons in the data, in square meters. Holes are subtracted. Points and lines have no area.

```javascript
getArea(data.features[0]); // 710.28... (Rektorat building)
getArea(data);             // 1980.88... (both buildings)
```

## `isInside(position, geojson)` and `getFeaturesAt(position, geojson)`

`isInside` answers `true`/`false`: whether the position lies inside any polygon in the data. `getFeaturesAt` returns the polygon features that contain it (an empty array if none), to find out *which polygon*.

```javascript
isInside([107.5761, -6.8735], data); // true
isInside([107.5759, -6.8736], data); // false (between the two buildings)

getFeaturesAt([107.5761, -6.8735], data).map((feature) => feature.properties.Gedung); // ["Auditorium"]
```

A point that falls inside a polygon's hole counts as outside that polygon.

## `getNearest(position, geojson)`

The point feature (`Point`/`MultiPoint`) closest to the position. Returns `{ feature, distance }`, or `null` if the data has no point features. Lines and polygons are not compared.

```javascript
const terdekat = getNearest([107.5761, -6.8735], data);
terdekat.feature.properties.Gedung; // "ULBI"
terdekat.distance;                  // 38.24...
```

## `createCircle(center, radius, steps = 64)`

Creates a circle-shaped polygon Feature centered at `center` with a radius of `radius` meters. GeoJSON has no notion of circles, so the result is a polygon with `steps` sides.

```javascript
const radiusPresensi = createCircle([107.575914, -6.8732098], 100); // 100 m circle
```

## `createAffineTransform(from, to)`

Creates an *affine* transformation (translate, rotate, scale, skew) from pairs of control points: the *i*-th point in `from` pairs with the *i*-th point in `to`, each `[x, y]`. Its purpose is converting local-system coordinates — a CAD grid, a building floor plan, the pixels of a scanned image — into `[lng, lat]`, and back.

It requires at least **3 non-collinear pairs**. More than 3 are fitted by least squares, so extra control points average out measurement errors.

Returns a function `transform([x, y])`, or `null` if there are too few control points, the counts don't match, or they are collinear. The function also has:

| Member | Content |
|---|---|
| `transform.inverse([x, y])` | The reverse direction: from the `to` system to the `from` system |
| `transform.error` | The mean (RMS) residual of the control points after transformation, in `to` units. For `[lng, lat]`, 0.00001° ≈ 1.1 m. A large value means a control point was mistyped |

```javascript
// Three survey markers with known project grid coordinates (meters) and lng/lat.
const grid = [[1000, 2000], [1500, 2000], [1000, 2400]];
const wgs84 = [[107.57520, -6.87410], [107.57974, -6.87407], [107.57517, -6.87048]];
const gridToWgs = createAffineTransform(grid, wgs84);

gridToWgs([1250, 2200]);                 // [lng, lat] of that grid point
gridToWgs.inverse([107.5775, -6.8723]);  // grid [x, y] from lng/lat
```

Converting an entire GeoJSON dataset from a CAD grid is just a matter of mapping each of its coordinates with `gridToWgs`. To place a floor plan image using control points, see `addImageOverlay` in [`maptools.js`](maptools).

An affine transform on `[lng, lat]` is accurate enough for district-sized areas (a few kilometers). For much larger regions, or data in an official projection such as UTM/TM-3, use the projection's formulas.

## Example: Location-Based Attendance

The most common combination: draw the radius, get the user's location, then check whether they are inside it.

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, fitMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { locateUser } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/mapcontrol.js";
import { createCircle, isInside, getDistance } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/geomeasure.js";

const kampus = [107.575914, -6.8732098];
const area = createCircle(kampus, 100);

createMap("peta");
addGeoJSON("peta", area);
fitMap("peta", area);

locateUser("peta", (lokasi) => {
    if (!lokasi) {
        console.log("Lokasi tidak didapat.");
        return;
    }
    if (isInside(lokasi.position, area)) {
        console.log("Di dalam area presensi.");
    } else {
        console.log(`Di luar area, ${Math.round(getDistance(lokasi.position, kampus))} m dari kampus.`);
    }
});
```

For areas that are not circular, replace `area` with the campus boundary polygon from your GeoJSON data; `isInside` works the same way.

## Notes

- All calculations treat the Earth as a sphere with a mean radius of 6,371,008.8 m — the same value Turf.js uses, so the numbers match Turf. The real Earth is slightly flattened, so results can be off by a few tenths of a percent from precise geodetic measurements. For distances and areas in everyday applications this is more than enough; for land boundaries or legal purposes, use proper surveying instruments.
- Device location has limited accuracy (see `accuracy` in [`mapcontrol.js`](mapcontrol)). For decisions like attendance, allow some tolerance: a point 5 m outside the boundary with 30 m accuracy is not necessarily truly outside.
- Data crossing the 180° meridian (antimeridian) is not handled specially.
- For routes along roads (not straight lines), see [`georoute.js`](georoute).


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/georoute

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../georoute)*

# `georoute.js` Module Documentation

`georoute.js` finds the **shortest route along the lines in your own GeoJSON data** — roads, alleys, campus paths, building corridors. The route is computed in the browser: no routing service is called, no API key is needed, and it keeps working offline as long as the data is already loaded.

This module is pure computation. It doesn't need a map; the result is plain GeoJSON that can be drawn with [`map.js`](map) or used as-is to get the travel distance.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { findRoute } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/georoute.js";
```

All [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure) functions (`getDistance`, `getLength`, `isInside`, and the rest) are also exported from `georoute.js`, so a page that computes routes only needs to import from here.

## `findRoute(from, to, geojson, options)`

Finds the shortest route from `from` to `to` (both `[lng, lat]`) along the `LineString` and `MultiLineString` geometries in `geojson`. Points and polygons in the data are ignored.

Returns a `Feature` with a `LineString` geometry and `properties.distance` holding the route length in meters — or `null` if the data has no lines, or the two points are not connected.

```javascript
const jalan = {
    type: "FeatureCollection",
    features: [
        { type: "Feature", properties: {}, geometry: { type: "LineString", coordinates: [[107.60, -6.90], [107.61, -6.90]] } },
        { type: "Feature", properties: {}, geometry: { type: "LineString", coordinates: [[107.61, -6.90], [107.61, -6.91]] } },
    ],
};

const rute = findRoute([107.604, -6.898], [107.612, -6.907], jalan);

rute.properties.distance;  // 1440.70... (meters)
rute.geometry.coordinates; // [[107.604, -6.9], [107.61, -6.9], [107.61, -6.907]]
```

In that example neither point lies exactly on a road. **`from` and `to` can be anywhere**: each is snapped to the nearest point on the nearest line, and the route starts and ends at those snapped points. So click coordinates or the user's location can be used directly.

## Drawing the Route on the Map

Since the result is a plain Feature, `addGeoJSON` can draw it directly:

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, fitMap, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/map.js";
import { findRoute } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.27/georoute.js";

createMap("peta");

getGeoJSON("jalan.geojson", (response) => {
    if (!response.data) return;

    const rute = findRoute([107.575914, -6.8732098], [107.5772, -6.8752], response.data);
    if (!rute) {
        console.log("Kedua titik tidak terhubung.");
        return;
    }
    addGeoJSON("peta", rute, { style: { stroke: "#2563eb", strokeWidth: 5 } });
    fitMap("peta", rute);
    console.log(`Panjang rute: ${Math.round(rute.properties.distance)} m`);
});
```

A complete example with draggable A and B pins: [demo](https://croot.js.org/examples/geo/route/) · [source](https://github.com/crootjs/examples/tree/main/geo/route).

## Data Requirement: Lines Must Meet at the Same Coordinate

Two lines are considered connected **only if they share the same coordinate** — at their ends or in the middle of a line. This is how OpenStreetMap road data is structured: every intersection is a single point shared by the roads that meet there.

As a result:

- Two lines that merely **cross** without a shared point are not connected. This is intentional: a flyover and the road beneath it also cross on the map, yet you cannot pass from one to the other.
- Two lines whose ends are merely **close together** (common in hand-drawn data) are not connected.

For the second case there is the `precision` option: the number of decimal places used when comparing coordinates. The smaller the value, the more loosely two points are considered equal.

| `precision` | Points are considered equal if they are roughly within |
|---|---|
| `6` (default) | 11 cm |
| `5` | 1 m |
| `4` | 11 m |

```javascript
findRoute(from, to, jalanGambarTangan, { precision: 5 });
```

If `findRoute` returns `null` even though the lines look connected on the map, this is almost always the cause. The cleanest fix is still to correct the data: when drawing, make sure lines that meet really share a single point.

## Notes

- **All lines are treated as two-way**, and what is searched for is the **shortest distance** — not the fastest time. One-way streets, turn restrictions, and speeds are not taken into account. This module suits pedestrian paths, campus areas, or your own networks; it is not a replacement for vehicle navigation.
- `properties.distance` is the length along the lines, from the starting snapped point to the ending snapped point. The distance from the `from`/`to` you provided to their snapped points is not included; compute it with [`getDistance`](geomeasure) if needed (for example to tell the user "your point is 300 m from the nearest road").
- The network is rebuilt on every call. In testing, a road extract with 252 segments was computed in a few milliseconds and a network of 22,500 intersections in about 0.1 seconds on a laptop; phones are slower. For city-scale data, crop the data to the area you need.
